families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Goblins are treated as a visual and encounter-production family, not as an accepted universal taxonomy. The packet preserves their short, wiry scavenger identity and violent loot hierarchy while expressing combat behavior as readable encounter roles.
families.escalationAxis: Scrap becomes treasure, and posture straightens from a cringing crouch to an upright swagger; rising forms turn stolen equipment into increasingly organized mob control, battlefield infrastructure, and finally a royal loot-production system.
visualConstants: Short, hunched, long-armed humanoid silhouette with an oversized head and pointed ears, disproportionately large hands and feet, hooked nose, and crowded crooked teeth.
Sickly green or gray-green skin against muddy browns, rust-orange, dull iron, and sparse accents of stolen gold.
Every carried object reads as stolen, scavenged, or crudely repaired: rags, patched leather, cracked wood, rusted scrap metal, bone, and rope rather than purpose-built matching equipment.
Loot is the status language: mismatched helmets, coin necklaces, teeth, rings, captured banners, and trophies accumulate with rank.
Posture and finish communicate hierarchy, from a knock-kneed cringing crouch to an upright swagger amid increasingly prestigious plunder.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Orcs are treated as a visual and encounter-production family, not as proof of universal culture, allegiance, morality, or personhood. This packet preserves their top-heavy anatomy, tusks, battle marks, heavy equipment, and visible status language while assigning each hostile form a specific authored combat duty.
families.escalationAxis: Tusks lengthen and curve higher as muscle, scars, iron, trophies, and command authority accumulate; rising forms turn committed heavy attacks into rhythmic pursuit, formation control, and finally an arena-wide trial of standards.
visualConstants: Tall, broad, top-heavy humanoid silhouette with a thick neck, wide shoulders, heavy jaw, forward lean, and lower tusks rising past the lip.
Gray-green or ash-gray skin is framed by blood red, black, dark iron, bone white, and readable red or white war paint.
Boiled leather, fur, riveted iron, bone, and crude steel remain thick, weighty, and practical rather than elegant or finely matched.
Scars, paint, tusk rings, piercings, skull trophies, spiked pauldrons, and clan totems communicate earned encounter rank without becoming a biological claim.
Tusk length, muscle mass, posture, and carried trophies escalate together, but every form retains committed heavy motion and exposed recovery as the family combat grammar.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Giants are treated as a scale-and-landscape production family rather than a claim that all enormous humanoids share one species, culture, or allegiance. The packet preserves humanlike heavy anatomy, progressive geology, rough mountain materials, and landscape scale while assigning encounter roles through committed weight and terrain displacement.
families.escalationAxis: Each tier expands both physical scale and the amount of lived-in geology across the body, converting a readable tree-club commitment into slope control, chained-megalith orbit, watershed command, and finally an arena that is itself a walking range.
visualConstants: Humanlike proportions scaled upward with a heavy brow, thick limbs, dense bone, and a slight stoop that communicates the body's own weight.
Stone gray, granite blue-gray, earth brown, moss green, glacier white, and warm amber eyes remain the family palette without requiring an elemental origin.
Rough hide, raw stone, moss, lichen, pine, iron chain, and rope accumulate as bodily geology and oversized practical tools.
Chains, standing-stone jewelry, skin runes, and whole trees function as ornament at a scale that stays legible from the arena.
Raw scale and geological coverage escalate together until the Sovereign carries a valley, but every form retains recognizable humanoid load paths and slow committed motion.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Trolls are treated as a regenerative body-horror production family, not as a claim that all cave, bridge, or bog dwellers share this physiology or hostility. The packet preserves their stooped long-armed anatomy, wet rubbery hide, visible mishealing, embedded debris, and accumulated scar history while giving each hostile form a bounded encounter role.
families.escalationAxis: Regeneration becomes increasingly visible and strategically wrong, progressing from one unstable wound cycle to lodged-injury pressure, player-steerable mutation, shed scar terrain, and a Sovereign that replays and produces its whole wound history.
visualConstants: Tall, stooped, potbellied humanoid silhouette with a small head on a thick neck and disproportionately long arms hanging past the knees.
Bog green, liver-brown, sallow gray, bruise purple, and wet glistening highlights keep living hide distinct from mud and scavenged rags.
Rubbery skin, scar tissue, bark-hard callus, mud, rope, and half-swallowed equipment remain visibly bodily rather than worn as deliberate finery.
Healed-over piercings, embedded bones, lodged weapons, misplaced limbs, stray jaws, and layered scars record prior injury as readable construction history.
Escalation adds accumulated misregrowth rather than simple size: open gashes become knots, alternate organs, defensive scar architecture, and finally a walking archive of incompatible healing.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Dragons are treated as a draconic visual and encounter-production family, not as a universal claim about intelligence, temperament, treasure ownership, or morality. The packet preserves long reptilian anatomy, four limbs plus age-dependent wings, horn and scale growth, territorial hoard materials, and direct silhouette-based maturation while assigning each hostile form a specific arena duty.
families.escalationAxis: Wings and horns mature from absent and unreliable to arena-defining structures, turning a ground pounce into short draft hops, authored flight lanes, hoard-shaped landing control, and a Sovereign circuit through every earlier movement grammar.
visualConstants: Long neck and tail, deep chest, four clawed limbs, wedge-shaped horned skull, and wings that emerge and expand after the wingless first form.
Each individual holds one coherent metallic or jewel-tone scale identity with a paler underbelly and bright reflective eyes, rather than changing base identity by affinity.
Overlapping scales, horn, bone spurs, and leathery wing membrane retain reptilian load paths and readable joints at every tier.
Horn crowns, spinal ridges, battle scars, torn membrane, and hoard metal fused into old belly scales accumulate as age and territorial history.
Wingspan and horn crown escalate together from absent wings and horn nubs to storm-front wings and branching imperial antlers, while the ground-to-sky grammar remains recognizable.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Skeletons are treated as a necromantically animated-remains production family, not as a biological species or evidence about the identity, autonomy, rights, or allegiance of the original dead. The packet preserves humanlike bone gaps, grave goods, socket-fire binding, progressive fusion, and cheap reassembly while assigning each hostile form an explicit battlefield duty.
families.escalationAxis: Loose bones become mail-bound ranks, a Specialist that levies battlefield fragments, fused spur architecture, and finally a royal sepulcher engine that commands, rebuilds, and promotes the whole skeletal court.
visualConstants: Human or humanoid skeletal proportions remain narrow, angular, and defined by empty negative space where flesh and organs would be.
Bone white or yellowed ivory is paired with rust, black iron, tattered grave-cloth, and one explained necromantic socket-fire accent such as green, blue, or gold.
Bone, rusted mail, corroded steel, grave-cloth, funerary jewelry, and crowns remain recognizable mortuary materials rather than living anatomy.
Carved skull runes, bone spurs, fused armor-like mass, grave regalia, and orbiting fragments accumulate as binding power becomes denser.
Bone density and the intensity and reach of the visible necromantic binding escalate together, but every form preserves gaps, joints, or binding anchors that can be deliberately broken.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Rotwalkers are treated as plague-animated human or humanoid corpses, not as a biological people or a claim about the identity, agency, morality, or allegiance of the deceased. Their family identity comes from wet opened remains, wrong-jointed posture, visible death wounds, and an animating rot that reverses decay into increasingly coordinated cohesion.
families.escalationAxis: The animating plague turns loose, death-marked remains into faster tendon systems, bone-bladed pressure, coordinated composite bodies, and a cathedral-like corpse sovereign that manufactures cohesion while preserving breakable seams.
visualConstants: A recognizably human but wrong silhouette retains dislocated shoulders, a dragging or mismatched gait, a hanging jaw, and a head or torso held at an impossible angle.
Gray-green and bruise-purple flesh, dried-blood brown, bile yellow, and dirty linen white remain bodily and funerary rather than elemental colors.
Rotting flesh, exposed sinew, wet bone, grave dirt, torn burial clothing, and the visible marks or embedded tools of death preserve each corpse's material history.
Every form is wet and partly open, with readable seams at tendons, ribs, sutures, or fused bodies that explain both animation and counterplay.
Escalation reverses decay into coordination: sagging fragments become corded muscle, reinforced bone, cooperative corpse anatomy, and finally a plague court built from many still-legible bodies.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Wraiths are treated as hostile incorporeal dead-person spirits for encounter production, not as a biological species or a universal statement about the dead, memory, autonomy, morality, or afterlife. Cold light, frost, and chill are family-native signs of deathly condensation in the source and remain explicitly non-affinity unless an authored elemental construction changes material and behavior.
families.escalationAxis: A barely held mist learns to drag anchors, weaponize the boundary between wall and room, spread a crowned cloak territory, and finally command a court through hollow regalia whose seals can be permanently opened.
visualConstants: A hooded or robed humanoid upper body becomes progressively defined while the lower body always trails into smoke or cold vapor without visible feet.
Black, charcoal, deep indigo, and ash gray carry one cold eye accent in pale blue, white, or sickly green; this family-native cold light is not an elemental affinity by itself.
Smoke, tattered shroud-cloth, cold vapor, rusted chain, and hollow armor preserve incorporeality through negative space and incomplete edges.
Chains, funeral shrouds, spectral crowns, and localized rings of source-native frost become anchors that explain when and where an otherwise incorporeal form can be opposed.
Escalation condenses a faint outline into a sharply defined regal silhouette while retaining a vapor tail, empty interior, and one readable anchor for every phase-through action.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Vampires are treated as intelligent blood-drinking undead whose authored encounter hierarchy is expressed through age and refinement, not as a biological race or a universal claim about culture, class, heredity, morality, consent, or personhood. Bestial posture, predatory anatomy, couture, crests, and blood-glass remain visual and mechanical production grammar rather than social canon.
families.escalationAxis: A hungry animal posture becomes a patient hunter, a formal blood-contract Specialist, a centuries-old cloak lord, and finally a crest-commanding throne sovereign whose shattered blood-glass court removes powers one lineage at a time.
visualConstants: A tall or lengthening human silhouette retains corpse-white skin, long fingers, fangs, claws, red eyes, and an absence of warm living complexion.
Posture escalates from feral hunch to impossible stillness; higher forms widen through fitted coats, tailored cloaks, bat membrane, or shadow wings without obscuring humanlike anatomy.
Black, bone pallor, deep blood red, and aged gold remain paired with velvet, silk, brocade, polished leather, blood-glass, and bat membrane.
Blood is family-native feeding matter and lineage symbolism rather than Fire or Water affinity by itself; every use has a source, route, vessel, or recoverable feeding window.
Signet rings, high collars, jeweled clasps, medals, canes, blades, and family crests communicate authored encounter rank while exposing the hand, vessel, or crest that carries each command.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Mummies are treated as ritually preserved, linen-wrapped dead whose grave goods and offices supply authored encounter ranks, not as a biological people or evidence about any real culture, religion, ethnicity, divinity, royal legitimacy, morality, or afterlife. Sand and dust are family-native burial residue and non-affinity staging; true affinities require separate material and behavior construction.
families.escalationAxis: Crude wrapping knots become bronze guard bindings, processional glyph circuits, a masked tomb formation, and a royal sarcophagus engine whose dismantled cartouches remove commands and unwrap a simpler final phase.
visualConstants: A stiff-limbed human or humanoid silhouette remains wrapped from head to foot, with arms held forward, crossed, guarding, inscribing, or commanding through readable linen tension.
Sun-bleached linen, sand beige, desert ocher, deep gold, lapis blue, and turquoise remain funerary materials and symbols rather than affinity colors.
Linen bandage, dried flesh, gold leaf, lapis, carnelian, bronze, and sandstone grave goods stay materially distinct and retain visible knots, stitches, glyph routes, and breakable seals.
Family-native sand and dust follow disturbed wrappings, tomb movement, and burial objects without becoming Earth or Wind affinity by themselves.
Escalation adds precious thread, glyph density, collars, masks, armor, headdresses, and sarcophagus regalia while the bandages never come off and always explain binding and counterplay.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Demons are treated as physically manifested underworld spirits organized into an authored hostile hierarchy, not as a biological people or a universal claim about religion, evil, culture, cognition, personhood, or social worth. Their source-native embers, magma, smoke, live fire, and obsidian are infernal body materials and non-affinity rank signs; Fire affinity must add a distinct engineered combustion grammar rather than duplicate that identity.
families.escalationAxis: A pest steals brands, a line Fiend spends them, a plated Hellknight sentences targets through a seal, an Archfiend chains the hierarchy into formation, and a throne-bound Prince promotes legions until broken command brands strip away its corona and court.
visualConstants: A horned head, broadening shoulders, digitigrade or hooved legs, long tail, claws, and bat-like wing membranes remain legible from cat-sized pest to enthroned sovereign.
Blood red or ashen hide, char black, source-native ember orange, molten yellow, and obsidian preserve an infernal body whose internal fire is explained anatomy rather than affinity by default.
Charred hide, obsidian, blackened iron, native molten rock, smoke, and bat membrane retain distinct surfaces instead of collapsing into a generic flame silhouette.
Brands, infernal sigils, chains, spiked black armor, skull motifs, and horn arrangements communicate authored rank and command routes without implying a universal moral taxonomy.

Horn count, wing authority, and the proportion of source-native fire or obsidian increase with rank, but every form preserves visible hide, joints, brand routes, and an interruptible hierarchy anchor.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Celestials are treated as winged beings manifested through light and geometric order for authored encounters, not as a biological people or a universal claim about religion, holiness, goodness, authority, moral worth, personhood, or cosmic law. Their light, sunlight colors, halos, and luminous bodies are family-native non-affinity materials and symbols; elemental variants require distinct construction beyond radiance.
families.escalationAxis: A two-wing Messenger draws one line, a Guardian braces it, a four-wing Warden rotates intersecting axes, a six-wing Archon composes those geometries, and an orrery Seraph commands and sheds entire ordered rings as the arena simplifies.
visualConstants: An idealized upright humanoid silhouette remains deliberately symmetrical, with feathered wings and a halo above or behind the head even as the body becomes increasingly abstract.
White, ivory, pale gold, sunlight yellow, and sky blue remain family-native ordered radiance rather than elemental affinity colors.
Polished gold, white marble, feather, silk, and source-native pure light stay layered so armor, cloth, wing roots, halo joints, and the suggested body remain readable.
Halos, ring geometry, sacred script, ribbons, censers, blank ceremonial masks, and wing count communicate rank through exact symmetry and moving parts rather than glow or size alone.
Escalation increases wing pairs and halo complexity from a simple ring to an orrery, but each tier preserves a breakable alignment joint and a learnable ordered command.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Harpies are treated as a winged visual and encounter-production family, not as an accepted taxonomy or a universal statement about sex, culture, cognition, personhood, social rank, or hostility. Their cliff-flock language becomes readable aerial combat roles while preserving the source anatomy and plumage escalation.
families.escalationAxis: Feather quality, talon reach, crest authority, and control of aerial lanes grow from a ragged noise probe into flock formations and a cliff-spanning sovereign storm court.
visualConstants: A humanoid torso remains joined to large raptor wings that replace or extend the arms, backward-jointed bird legs, oversized talons, and a feathered head crest.
Slate gray, brown, and dirty cream mature into iridescent blue-green, storm purple, and white without losing the family feather pattern.
Feather, hollow bone, sinew, raw hide, braided hair, and gold ankle ornaments remain physically readable materials.
Bone jewelry, trophy feathers, braided hair, ankle rings, and crest height communicate status without changing the core wing-and-talon silhouette.
Every attack keeps the wing roots, talons, crest, and flight direction visible enough to preserve counterplay.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Minotaurs are treated as a horned visual and encounter-production family, not as an accepted biological people or a universal statement about culture, intelligence, rank, blood sport, or hostility. Labyrinth and arena imagery becomes authored battlefield geometry rather than an assumed social identity.
families.escalationAxis: Horn spread, visible arena history, and weapon mass escalate from a rangy maul carrier to a sovereign who reconfigures a shattered arena through gateway-wide horn arcs.
visualConstants: A bull head, bovine snout and ears, wide horns, vastly overbuilt humanoid torso, digitigrade hooved legs, and thick tail remain legible at every tier.
Deep russet and black hide, bronze, ox-blood red, and bone define the family palette.
Coarse hair, horn, bronze, heavy leather harness, chain, and hewn stone remain distinct load-bearing materials.
Nose rings, horn caps, brands, arena trophies, and chained slabs communicate rank through visible history and repairs.
Weapon mass and horn spread always preserve a readable commitment direction and recovery side.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Nagas are treated as a serpentine visual and encounter-production family, not as an accepted people or a universal statement about culture, antiquity, intelligence, religion, guardianship, sacred water, treasure, or forbidden knowledge. Temple imagery supplies authored mechanisms while the packet leaves taxonomy, belief, and personhood unresolved.
families.escalationAxis: Coil length, scale ornament, temple mechanism authority, hood complexity from T3 onward, and hand count grow from a mobile two-armed skirmisher to a sovereign relic court.
visualConstants: A humanoid torso rises from a long coiled serpent body; the T1–T2 forms have two arms and no hood, while hood and additional arms begin only at T3.
Emerald, jade, deep teal, gold, bronze, ivory, and jewel-toned scale patterns remain the family palette.
Scale, gold, gemstone inlay, silk sash, and temple stone remain separate readable materials rather than a seamless magical body.
Arm bands, gold scale bands, jeweled brow pieces, sacred script, and later hood crests communicate rank.
Coil direction, weapon-bearing hands, hood angle where present, and exposed scale seams preserve attack and counterplay readability.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Lizardfolk are treated as a reptilian visual and encounter-production family, not as an accepted biological people or a universal statement about culture, technology, intelligence, social rank, personhood, habitat, or hostility. Source swamp and tribal imagery becomes explicit equipment and arena grammar rather than essentialized identity.
families.escalationAxis: Crest height, dorsal spines, natural plating, tail weaponization, and control of marked hunting ground grow from a lean scout to a sovereign back-sail war court.
visualConstants: An upright forward-leaning reptilian body keeps clawed hands and feet, a long counterbalancing tail, a crocodilian or iguana-like head, and an escalating dorsal ridge.
Swamp green, mud brown, moss, and ocher are punctuated by warning-bright orange, red, or yellow throat and crest colors.
Scale, bone, obsidian, hide, river reed, ordinary mud, and feather remain separately legible materials.
Paint, bone piercings, trophy skulls, woven shields, and feather headdresses accumulate without obscuring natural plating.
Tail angle, crest posture, dorsal plates, hands, and planted feet preserve the direction and recovery of each attack.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Insectoids are treated as a chitinous visual and encounter-production family, not as an accepted people or universal claims about intelligence, caste, cognition, individuality, personhood, reproductive role, social organization, or hostility. Hive and caste language becomes authored combat coordination while every biological and cultural claim remains a proposal pending taxonomy review.
families.escalationAxis: Caste specialization, chitin gloss, limb purpose, vent and wing development, and authority over wax-comb routes grow from a worker probe to a stationary production sovereign.
visualConstants: Segmented chitinous body, mandibled head, compound eyes, four to six limbs, narrow waist, and rear abdomen remain legible across all forms.
Chitin brown and black mature into glossy crimson, iridescent green-black, and amber accents without replacing caste-specific limb shapes.
Chitin, resin, wax comb, translucent wing membrane where anatomically present, and amber remain distinct family materials.
Shell ridging, fluting, resin plating, spiracle vents, and comb-throne structures communicate specialization rather than generic size.
Wing state is tier-specific: T1–T2 have no wings, T3 has closed wing cases, T4 has functional wings, and the immense T5 Queen is wingless.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Arachnids are treated as a spider-bodied visual and encounter-production family, not as an accepted biological people or universal claims about intelligence, culture, rank, personhood, habitat, predation, or hostility. The T1–T2 remain oversized spiders; the humanoid torso begins only at T3 and is treated as a designed form transition pending taxonomy review.
families.escalationAxis: Eye organization, leg span, silk refinement, web topology, and command over brood routes grow from a hunting spider to a cathedral-scale sovereign loom.
visualConstants: A bulbous abdomen, eight jointed legs arching around the body, clustered eyes, fangs, and spinnerets remain legible; a humanoid torso is added only from T3 onward.
Black, charcoal, deep violet, blood-red markings, pale silk white, and green, red, or amber eye accents form the source palette.
Chitin, coarse bristle, silk, bone, amber, venom sheen, and eye settings remain physically distinct family materials.
Web decorations, silk robes, egg sacs, wrapped prey, jeweled eye settings, and layered drapery communicate escalation.
Leg load, spinneret direction, fang posture, silk tension, and eye cluster alignment preserve readable attack and recovery states.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Slimes are treated as an amorphous visual and encounter-production family, not as accepted claims about biology, cognition, feeding, agency, personhood, or universal hostility. Engulfing and digestion are encounter proposals; the packet preserves gravity-led jelly, visible contents, and a core weak point while humanoid structure begins only at T3.
families.escalationAxis: Internal structure and battlefield coordination emerge from formlessness, culminating in a multicore sovereign that redistributes its own mass through lesser slimes.
visualConstants: Rounded, drooping, gravity-obeying jelly with surface-tension edges and a readable internal core remains the family silhouette.
Translucent blue, acid green, amber, or violet is chosen per individual, with suspended debris and a brighter but bounded core.
Viscous flow, drip trails, swallowed objects, crystalline cores, and later crust plates remain spatially coherent.
Internal structure emerges by tier: pseudopod, debris-bearing blob, humanoid crust frame, suspended skeleton, then a multicore tide.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Golems are treated as a constructed visual and encounter-production family. Statements about servitude, animation, life, free will, makers, rank, and agency are proposals rather than accepted metaphysics or social taxonomy. The packet preserves blocky workmanship progression and readable magical joints without asserting universal personhood.
families.escalationAxis: Workmanship, material quality, and programmable rune behaviors rise from crude clay to a sovereign monument that reconfigures the arena.
visualConstants: Blocky heavy humanoid construction, oversized hands, small or absent head, blank carved face, and visible joint gaps remain legible.
Clay, fieldstone, iron banding, granite, basalt, marble, gold inlay, and gemstone stay distinct construction materials.
Runes and seam light remain bounded animation hardware rather than generic affinity spectacle.
Workmanship and material quality progress from fingerprints and one scratched rune to sculptural relief and a gemstone heart.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Elementals are treated as magical entities whose temporary bodies take on unaffiliated spell-matter or one of the four base affinities. This is a visual and encounter-production family, not an accepted claim about origin, life, cognition, agency, personhood, summoning, or hostility. A flame-like outer contour describes shape and motion only; it does not imply Fire affinity.
families.escalationAxis: Form coherence, core complexity, and control over shaped affinity substance rise from one drifting teardrop to a sovereign that transforms the arena through four learned binding patterns.
visualConstants: Every form is organized around one readable binding seed or core, with no flesh, worn armor, ordinary clothing, handheld weapon, or fixed face.
The T1 Wisp is a small asymmetric teardrop or flame-like shape without limbs; T2–T5 develop a legless hovering upper body with exactly two coherent arm channels and a tapering lower body.
Affinity substance forms the complete load-bearing body, limbs, mantle, and directional wake rather than appearing as a colored exterior aura or decorative overlay.
Form coherence, core structure, and spatial control progress from one wandering Wisp to a four-facet Sovereign while the active telegraph and exposed counterplay remain readable.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Treants are treated as a walking-tree visual and encounter-production family. Claims about age, status, society, cognition, agency, personhood, habitat, and universal behavior remain proposals pending taxonomy review. Ordinary tree material, roots, moss, water, and caught stone are family-native botany and history, not affinity labels.
families.escalationAxis: Age and ecosystem load turn simple root movement into canopy control and finally a sovereign walking forest that reconfigures the arena.
visualConstants: Vertical trunk body, root-cluster legs, long branch arms, a bark-suggested face, and canopy remain recognizable.
Bark brown and gray, moss green, autumn gold, sap, and restrained amber heartwood remain botanical materials.
Nests, vines, mushrooms, bark runes, scars, and growth rings record age without replacing readable joints.
Girth, canopy, rooted reach, and resident ecosystems escalate while branch load and root commitment preserve counterplay.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Fungalfolk are treated as a mushroom-bodied visual and encounter-production family. Claims about habitat, communication, society, cognition, agency, personhood, reproduction, rank, and universal behavior are proposals pending taxonomy review. Bioluminescence, spores, mycelium, and damp surroundings are native fungal motifs rather than affinities.
families.escalationAxis: Cap reach and network control progress from a dust puff to battlefield spore writing and finally a sovereign throne connected to the arena floor.
visualConstants: Cap-headed, stalk-bodied silhouette with gills, bulbous limbs, and a wider top than base remains recognizable.
Pale fungal flesh and one strong cap tone contrast with bounded cyan or green gill bioluminescence from T2 onward.
Fungal flesh, spongy cap, mycelium, damp moss, and spore dust remain organic and spatially coherent.
Cap breadth, gill light, spore density, secondary growth, and ground mycelium escalate at explicit source tiers.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Deep Ones are treated as a pressure-adapted aquatic visual and encounter-production family. Claims about ancestry, worship, society, raiding, cognition, age, agency, personhood, and hostility are proposals pending taxonomy review. Ocean wetness, coral, native lures, and bioluminescence preserve source identity without making every form Water-affined.
families.escalationAxis: Pressure adaptation and deep-sea command progress from a gasping raider to a sovereign whose court and kraken limbs divide the arena.
visualConstants: Hunched long-armed humanoid silhouette, wide flat head, lidless eyes, gill-neck, fins, webbed claws, and needle teeth remain legible.
Drowned green, deep-sea blue-black, sickly gray, pearlescent white, and bounded cold native light form the source palette.
Wet scale, eel skin, coral, barnacle, driftwood, rusted metal, whale bone, net, pearl, and shell remain distinct materials.
Pressure bulk, loss of familiar humanoid proportion, and native light-bearing anatomy escalate at explicit source tiers.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Werebeasts are treated as a staged hybrid-transformation visual and encounter-production family. Claims about human origin, curse, permanence, culture, cognition, agency, personhood, and hostility remain proposals pending taxonomy review.
families.escalationAxis: The visible degree and permanence of hybrid transformation advances from an afflicted human probe to a sovereign that commands staged transformations.
visualConstants: A human frame progressively stretches toward animal proportions while hands, shoulders, legs, muzzle, and tail change at explicit tiers.
Gray, black, russet, or silver fur remains distinct from torn muted human clothing, hide, iron restraints, claw, and fang.
Shredded dress, snapped restraints, ritual scars, and restrained moon motifs record the unfinished transformation without defining an affinity.
Loss of human proportion escalates from patchy changes to an authored sovereign transformation while readable joints remain exposed.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Gargoyles are treated as an animated architectural-statue visual and encounter-production family. Claims about origin, night behavior, duty, rank, cognition, agency, personhood, and hostility remain proposals pending taxonomy review.
families.escalationAxis: Material refinement and wing architecture progress from a perched chipped ornament to a sovereign architecture that commands its own statuary court.
visualConstants: Squat crouched construction, hunched shoulders, horned beast face, clawed grip, and folded architectural wings remain recognizable.
Sandstone, granite, marble, bronze, mortar, moss, and water staining remain discrete built materials rather than flesh.
Relief carving, water-spout mouths, restrained amber seams, and pedestal fragments preserve the architectural source grammar.
Stone quality and wing architecture escalate from useless carved flaps to sovereign buttresses while load-bearing joints stay readable.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Djinn are treated as a bound smoke-bodied spirit visual and encounter-production family. Claims about air identity, fire identity, spirit identity, binding, wishes, culture, rank, cognition, agency, personhood, and hostility remain proposals pending taxonomy review.
families.escalationAxis: Increasingly coherent command over a smoke body and proposed binding ornaments advances from a small vapor probe to a sovereign lamp-court vortex.
visualConstants: A hovering humanoid upper body tapers into smoke instead of legs; solidity and scale change only at explicit tiers.
Sapphire or violet smoke, warm inner light, gold, brass, turquoise, silk, and gemstones remain distinct source materials.
Cuffs, rings, headpieces, lamps, and script mark proposed binding status without establishing universal culture or morality.
The body becomes less solid and more spatially dominant from half-face vapor to a palace-scale throne vortex.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Fae are treated as a progressively alien wild-growth spirit visual and encounter-production family. Claims about wild-wood origin, beauty, friendliness, court, culture, cognition, agency, personhood, and hostility remain proposals pending taxonomy review. Leaf, bark, and branch are ordinary source materials, not a current retired botanical element label.
families.escalationAxis: Wing construction, scale, court ornament, and perceptual strangeness progress from a thorn-bearing sprite to a season-transforming sovereign.
visualConstants: A slender weightless-looking silhouette retains layered wings while scale, head growth, and proportion change only at explicit tiers.
Spring green, petal pink, dusk violet, moth iridescence, and bounded gold pollen light remain source palette rather than affinity evidence.
Living leaf, petal, spider silk, stained glass, bark, dew, and moth wing remain discrete ordinary or uncanny materials.
Wing complexity and subtly wrong beauty escalate from a palm sprite to a sovereign whose geometry bends the surrounding frame.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Void Horrors are treated as a progressively unresolved absence-and-fracture visual and encounter-production family. Claims about extradimensional origin, ontology, intent, cognition, agency, personhood, and hostility remain proposals pending taxonomy review.
families.escalationAxis: Coherence is progressively subtracted from a thin-limbed crawler until the sovereign is an unresolved world-shaped absence with one readable eye-ring system.
visualConstants: Rough humanoid or many-limbed absence retains edges that fail to close while proportions shift only within readable tier silhouettes.
Matte void black, negative space, purple-black, star flecks, and one bounded cold eye accent remain source grammar rather than affinity evidence.
Absence, non-reflection, star-field interior, fractured geometry, eye rings, and geometric shards never resolve into ordinary flesh or matter.
Power subtracts coherence: later forms occupy less resolvable physical presence while telegraph anchors become deliberately sparse.

families.classificationNotes: Source-draft Doppelgangers are treated as a copy-quality and leaking-disguise visual and encounter-production family. Claims about infiltration, motive, social behavior, cognition, agency, personhood, and hostility remain proposals pending taxonomy review.
families.escalationAxis: Copy fidelity and the number of simultaneous borrowed identities advance from blank smooth flesh to a body-wide sovereign mask procession.
visualConstants: A generic humanoid copy silhouette retains one deliberate flaw until layered face and mask motifs appear at explicit upper tiers.
Clay-gray skin, putty, borrowed colors, porcelain, copied cloth, and smooth flesh remain discrete source materials rather than Earth affinity.
Seams, wrong joints, ill-fitting clothes, and layered masks reveal copy quality while preserving the readable original-copy relationship.
Disguise fidelity escalates from an entirely blank true form to a sovereign carrying many stolen-looking faces at once.

families.classificationNotes: A natural lupine expedition family built around pack geometry, pursuit, and coordinated prey selection. It remains distinct from transformed humanoid Werebeasts.
families.escalationAxis: Opportunistic flanking becomes alternating pursuit, directional pack timing, marked-prey command, and finally an arena-scale hunt circle controlled by an apex Greatwolf.
visualConstants: Every form retains a four-legged lupine skeleton, long muzzle, visible paws, expressive ears, and a readable tail; no form becomes humanoid or wears manufactured armor.
Rank is communicated through chest mass, coat mantle, scars, posture, and pack behavior rather than arbitrary glow or simple scale.
Pack attack direction remains readable through gaze, ear position, tail line, paw placement, and the spacing of companion Wolves.

families.classificationNotes: A natural ursine expedition family built around mass, committed attacks, grappling, and territorial control.
families.escalationAxis: A simple committed swipe becomes frontal maul pressure, an asymmetric hook-and-drag specialist, terrain-breaking dominance, and finally den-scale territorial command.
visualConstants: Every form retains a four-legged ursine body, plantigrade paws, compact tail, broad muzzle, dense coat, and weight-bearing shoulder hump.
Escalation uses coat condition, scars, claw specialization, posture, and environmental interaction rather than humanoid equipment.
Raised shoulders, planted hind legs, open chest, and exposed inner wrists preserve readable commitment and recovery windows.

families.classificationNotes: A natural suid expedition family centered on predictable charge lanes, bracing, displacement, and route creation.
families.escalationAxis: A short straight charge becomes a braced line-breaker, curved furrow specialist, formation-opening champion, and three-lane sovereign stampede.
visualConstants: Every form keeps a low four-legged boar body, cloven hooves, mobile snout, raised bristles, short tail, and visible tusk roots.
Tier escalation uses tusk geometry, neck mass, shoulder callus, scars, and bristle profile rather than humanoid equipment.
Charge direction remains readable through hoof placement, lowered head angle, tusk contact, dust, and the alignment of the spine.

families.classificationNotes: One segmented subterranean animal lineage built around ground reading, eruption timing, towing, false ridges, and tunnel networks. It is not a miscellaneous bin for unrelated cave creatures.
families.escalationAxis: A single moving ridge becomes a long eruption lane, hookjaw towing specialist, decoy-ridge champion, and persistent tunnel-network sovereign.
visualConstants: Every form retains a limbless segmented body, armored digging front, softer articulated rear, tactile sensory organs, and soil-displacing locomotion.
Tier is shown through mandible specialization, segment reinforcement, collar structure, tail shape, and tunneling behavior rather than humanoid traits.
The real underground route and the exposed punish segment always have physical environmental tells.

families.classificationNotes: A natural feline expedition family centered on concealment, facing, isolation, explosive pounces, and hunting-territory control.
families.escalationAxis: A simple cover pounce becomes high-ground hunting, sightline isolation, saber-tooth pinning, and finally an apex territory hunt that assigns every lower form a role.
visualConstants: Every form retains a four-legged feline body, flexible spine, retractile claws, whiskered muzzle, mobile ears, and expressive tail.
Species variation remains feline and is communicated by coat pattern, limb proportion, mane, canine length, and hunting posture rather than equipment.
Eye line, tail stillness, shoulder compression, cover disturbance, and landing posture preserve readable attack direction.

families.classificationNotes: A natural limbless snake family centered on fixed strike range, constriction, venom lanes, buried reach, and living coil control. It remains distinct from sapient humanoid Nagas.
families.escalationAxis: A fixed one-length strike becomes anchored constriction, a two-lane venom specialist, buried alternating reach, and finally a sovereign whose body coils become arena terrain.
visualConstants: Every form remains limbless with a continuous scaled body, snake skull, jaw hinge, belly scutes, forked tongue, and species-appropriate tail.
Tier escalation uses body proportion, hood, fangs, horns, crown scales, muscle distribution, and coil behavior rather than arms or equipment.
Strike range, head anchor, venom direction, emergence point, and loosened coil remain visually traceable.

families.classificationNotes: A natural quadrupedal reptile family centered on shoreline risk, armored facing, clamping, bank drags, death rolls, and floodplain control. It remains distinct from humanoid Lizardfolk and winged Dragons.
families.escalationAxis: A single waterline snap becomes a backward clamp, lateral bank-drag specialist, armored death-roll champion, and floodplain sovereign controlling multiple channels.
visualConstants: Every form retains a low four-legged crocodilian body, long tail, scuted back, belly fault, sensory pits, and a jaw-driven attack silhouette.
Tier escalation uses snout geometry, scute height, neck mobility, tail mass, scars, and waterline behavior rather than equipment or wings.
Eyes, wake direction, jaw angle, foreclaw grooves, tail curve, and exposed belly keep ambush and rotation counterplay readable.

families.classificationNotes: A natural bird-of-prey family centered on vertical tracking, attack shadows, landing windows, carry threats, and airspace control. It remains distinct from humanoid Harpies.
families.escalationAxis: A single shadow dive becomes alternating perch attacks, silent movement-triggered drops, carry-off pressure, and finally a sovereign that divides the arena into flight bands.
visualConstants: Every form retains an avian body with two wings, two taloned legs, hooked beak, feathered tail, and species-appropriate head rather than humanoid arms or torso.
Tier escalation uses wingspan, feather structure, facial disc, talon mass, scars, and flight behavior rather than worn equipment.
Shadow shape, tail fan, primary-feather angle, talon extension, perch choice, and landing route keep aerial attacks readable.

monsters.name: Runt
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Flood open flanks, crowd isolated targets, and force the player to create breathing room before stronger Goblins arrive.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that a lone Runt is brittle but a cluster gains nerve, so early crowd separation is safer than trading inside the mob.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Mob Nerve: the Runt stops cringing and makes rapid stick jabs only while shoulder-to-shoulder with another Goblin; when separated, it hesitates and backs toward the nearest ally.
monsters.telegraph: Its knees straighten, ears lift, and the sharpened stick rises from a defensive clutch when another Goblin enters arm's reach.
monsters.counterplay: Displace or quickly remove one member of the cluster; the remaining Runt visibly cringes, pauses its jab chain, and can be cleared before it regroups.

monsters.name: Cutter
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Hold a messy front line by pinning one target in place while Runts crowd the exposed sides.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the repeatable Goblin formation: the best-equipped bully fixes attention while weaker bodies make the formation dangerous.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Bully's Hook: the Cutter catches clothing or guard with the notch in its cleaver and leans back, slowing the target while any adjacent Runt gains Mob Nerve from the protected position.
monsters.telegraph: It drops its oversized helmet over its eyes, turns the cleaver notch inward, and plants one foot before the hook.
monsters.counterplay: Sidestep the narrow hook, strike during the helmet-blind recovery, or push the Cutter away from its Runts to collapse both the pin and their Mob Nerve.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Shelters Runts behind its leather-scrap side and deliberately holds hooked targets where their stick jabs can reach.

monsters.name: Raider
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Change the shape of the encounter by carrying mobile cover into a firing lane, then planting it as a temporary barricade that creates a Goblin advance route.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the qualitative Specialist pivot: the first nearly upright, well-equipped Goblin is dangerous because it edits space and formation access, not because it is merely tougher.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Claimed Door: the Raider braces its scavenged door shield through incoming fire, then slams the lower edge into the ground to create one-way cover for smaller Goblins; planting commits the shield and leaves the sword arm and back exposed.
monsters.telegraph: It turns the door broadside, peers through a hacked eye slot, and drags a bright rope brace taut before the ground-slam.
monsters.counterplay: Interrupt before the rope locks, flank the exposed sword side after planting, cut the visible brace to topple the door, or force the Raider away so the claimed lane no longer advances with it.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Runts and Cutters stream behind the planted door; a Cutter can hold its brace while the Raider leaves cover to flank, making the brace carrier a readable way to collapse the formation.

monsters.name: Warboss
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Claim and patrol a rally zone, combining mob nerve, pins, and door cover into an organized push while personally punishing anyone who attacks the formation head-on.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach commander prioritization: lower forms become an army only while the Warboss's trophy standard defines a rally zone, but the hulking champion guards that standard with committed sweeps.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Helm-Tree Rally: the Warboss plants its banner of enemy helms, straightening nearby Goblins and letting their formation mechanics persist at greater spacing; it answers attacks on the banner with a slow, armor-weighted cleave that cannot turn once committed.
monsters.telegraph: The stolen helms clatter down the pole, nearby Goblins snap upright, and the Warboss flashes its gold teeth before hauling the chestplate and weapon into a fixed sweeping stance.
monsters.counterplay: Bait the fixed cleave away from the pole, attack from its trailing side, then topple the banner or pull lower forms beyond its marked trophy radius before they reform.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Runts retain Mob Nerve across the rally zone, Cutters pin intruders at its edge, and Raiders angle their planted doors toward the banner; removing the banner returns every interaction to its shorter, local form.

monsters.name: Goblin King
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Operate a command-and-production boss encounter that converts carried battlefield scrap into reinforcements, promotions, and repaired formation tools while issuing role-specific orders from the royal dais.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of the whole family by making the player read which production station and decree is coming, sever its supply chain, and dismantle lower-form formations before confronting the dismounted King.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Royal Lootworks: the welded throne-dais has three exposed stations fueled by scrap that Cutters deliver. At each command beat the King points to one station: the cage winch brings fresh Runts from a warren hatch, the armory chute outfits a surviving Runt as a Cutter, or the door press repairs a Raider's broken Claimed Door. Between cycles, a captured-flag decree orders Runts to rush, Cutters to collect, Raiders to barricade, and any Warboss to defend the active station. Destroyed stations stay disabled and loss of all three forces the King off the throne.
monsters.telegraph: The King rises beneath the crown of fused crowns, points a ring-heavy hand, and yanks one captured flag; the selected station's stolen bell rings while its gears visibly spool and the matching lower forms shout and turn toward their ordered route.
monsters.counterplay: Intercept scrap-carrying Cutters, cut the bright drive rope before the bell finishes, destroy the exposed selected station, or lure its defenders away; each broken station removes one production option, and an empty dais makes the dismounted King fight without replacement troops or repaired doors.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Cutters carry dropped scrap to power the throne; Runts arrive through the cage winch and can be outfitted into Cutters; Raiders receive repaired door shields and execute barricade decrees; a Warboss rallies defenders around whichever station the King has activated.

monsters.name: Grunt
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe the front line with a short spear or hand-axe rush that displaces a guarded target but leaves the lean attacker stranded if the rush misses.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the Orc family's basic bargain: broad shoulders and heavy intent make the approach dangerous, while planted feet and a forward lean make the recovery readable and punishable.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Shoulder Test: the Grunt lowers one hide-wrapped shoulder behind its crude weapon and drives straight through the first occupied space; contact shoves both combatants, while a miss carries the Grunt past the target before it can turn.
monsters.telegraph: It scrapes one bare foot backward, tucks its small blunt tusks, and draws the spear or axe tight beside the lowered shoulder.
monsters.counterplay: Step across the narrow line rather than retreating, then strike the unarmored ribs or back while the Grunt plants its forward foot and turns.

monsters.name: Warrior
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Maintain reliable line pressure by using an iron-banded shoulder check to open a guard, then occupying the breach with a controlled heavy-axe follow-through.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read paint and stance as a two-beat sequence: the red eye-band signals the advancing shoulder, while the first scars and axe angle reveal which side will be exposed afterward.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Red-Line Breach: the Warrior smears fresh paint down one axe cheek, checks forward behind iron-banded leather, then sweeps toward the painted side; the second beat occurs only if the shoulder makes contact.
monsters.telegraph: It drags two fingers through the red band across its eyes, marks one axe cheek, and turns the matching shoulder forward.
monsters.counterplay: Dodge to the unpainted side or stop the shoulder before contact; either response cancels the sweep and exposes the Warrior's underarm while the heavy axe resets.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: A Warrior can stop beside an overextended Grunt and use the Grunt's spear line as the edge of its breach, but separating their lanes prevents the paired shove-and-sweep.

monsters.name: Berserker
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Turn a stable front into a moving tempo hazard by chaining alternating twin-cleaver lanes and forcing the player to interrupt cadence rather than merely retreat from a tougher attacker.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the qualitative Specialist pivot: the Berserker's threat comes from an authored left-right rhythm encoded in its scar lattice and pauldrons, and breaking that rhythm is safer than outrunning it.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Scar-Lattice Bloodbeat: each cleaver strike follows the next diagonal of the chest scar lattice, alternating sides and widening the pursuit arc; completing three beats triggers a crossed finishing chop, but a clean interruption or a miss resets the sequence and leaves both arms spread.
monsters.telegraph: One spiked pauldron rolls forward, the matching cleaver taps a bright scar intersection, and the chest expands on a clearly countable beat before each diagonal advance.
monsters.counterplay: Cross behind the pauldron that just moved, force one beat to miss against open space or terrain, or interrupt on the visible scar tap; the reset exposes the unplated scar lattice before the cleavers can recross.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Grunts and Warriors try to hold targets inside the next marked diagonal, but their bodies also block the Berserker's widening route and can be used to force a sequence-breaking miss.

monsters.name: Warchief
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Plant and rotate a clan front around a skull totem, ordering committed attacks into complementary lanes while guarding the command point with paired greataxes.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach commander prioritization: lower Orcs lose their coordinated recoveries when the totem falls, but the Warchief's fixed two-axe answer makes a frontal assault on it a deliberate trap.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Totem Turn: the Warchief rotates the skull totem toward one arena quarter, causing Grunts to shoulder-test inward, Warriors to breach across them, and Berserkers to begin Bloodbeat along the painted boundary; the Warchief then locks both greataxes into a slow crossing guard that cannot pivot away from that quarter.
monsters.telegraph: The gate-sized iron rings on its tusks strike together, the skull totem tips toward a painted quarter, and every nearby Orc turns its marked shoulder or scar lattice along the same boundary.
monsters.counterplay: Move against the indicated rotation, bait the fixed crossing guard into empty space, then cut the totem lashings from the rear; without it, lower forms resume local tells and no longer cover one another's recoveries.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: The totem assigns lanes to Grunts, Warriors, and Berserkers and shortens their exposed resets only while they face its selected quarter; its loss breaks the formation into independent attacks.

monsters.name: Overlord
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a phased arena trial in which captured standards define challenge lanes, surviving lower forms earn transformations into the next duty, and the Overlord personally enforces whichever standard remains standing.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of commitment, breach sides, Bloodbeat rhythm, and totem rotation by making players choose which visible standard to disable before its trial promotes the Orc formation.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Trial of Standards: the Overlord plants three enemy standards around a central ribcage throne and impales one with its banner-pole to begin a trial. The Rush standard sends Grunts through narrow shoulder lanes and promotes a survivor into a Warrior; the Red standard pairs Warriors into crossing breaches and marks a survivor as a Berserker; the Skull standard lets a Warchief rotate every remaining lane. Breaking a standard permanently removes that trial. After each break, the Overlord tears one rib plate from its great-beast armor to wield as a curved arena gate, changing the remaining routes rather than simply gaining power.
monsters.telegraph: The dagger-long tusks hook a chosen standard, the cloak of hides swings toward its painted lane, and the matching lower forms strike weapons or scars in unison while one rib plate visibly unlocks from the armor.
monsters.counterplay: Read the selected standard, defeat or displace its designated survivor before promotion, attack the standard during the Overlord's committed enforcement sweep, and use each removed rib gate to block the next trial lane; destroying all standards ends promotions and forces a direct final duel with permanently opened armor seams.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Grunts, Warriors, Berserkers, and any Warchief receive standard-specific routes and promotion duties; players can deny those transformations, and every destroyed standard permanently removes one category of lower-form command.

monsters.name: Brute
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Clear a broad but slow front with a tree-trunk club, leaving the fallen timber as a temporary obstacle that changes one simple route through the arena.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the Giant family's readable mass: watch the heels and hands to identify a committed arc, leave it early, then use the displaced landscape during the long recovery.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Timber Fall: the Brute grips its tree trunk at one end and drops the full length across a marked lane; the club remains grounded until the Giant walks its hands down and lifts again, creating cover on one side and an exposed hand on the other.
monsters.telegraph: Its weathered hands slide to the trunk's far end, the rear heel digs a dark crescent in the soil, and the bare shoulder rises beneath the weight.
monsters.counterplay: Cross behind the planted heel before the trunk falls, then strike the grounded hand or use the fallen timber to block the Brute's shortest turn.

monsters.name: Hill Giant
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Apply repeatable ranged pressure by hauling and releasing rope-cradled boulders down selected lanes, then occupying the new low ground behind them.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that Giant terrain attacks have visible load paths: the rope belt, shoulder moss, and first back plates show where the boulder is tied and which slope will carry it.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Hill Roll: the Giant unhooks one boulder from its rope belt, braces it against a forming back plate, and releases it along the lower of two visible slopes; the empty rope loop then drags behind and can be stepped on during retrieval.
monsters.telegraph: Moss sheds from one shoulder, the corresponding rope loop pulls taut, and the Giant tests the ground with a broad foot before turning the boulder downhill.
monsters.counterplay: Move to higher ground or behind the dropped tree cover, then pin or cut the empty dragging loop before the Giant retrieves another boulder.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: A Brute can knock a stalled boulder into a new line with Timber Fall, but the same trunk can wedge the roll if the player draws the two attacks together.

monsters.name: Stone Giant
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Replace simple linear sweeps with a moving circular exclusion zone, using a chained megalith to divide the arena and pull displaced terrain into a deliberate orbit.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the qualitative Specialist pivot: read chain geometry, move through the quiet center rather than away from raw size, and punish the fixed pivot when the megalith changes orbit.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Megalith Orbit: the Stone Giant anchors the chain around a boulder-ridged forearm and walks a measured circle, swinging the megalith through a wide outer ring while the space beside its cliff-face brow remains calm. Reversing direction requires the Giant to plant the megalith, step across the chain, and expose the anchor wrist.
monsters.telegraph: Iron chain rises link by gate-sized link, the megalith scrapes a bright circular track, and runes along one forearm align toward the intended orbit before the first swing.
monsters.counterplay: Enter the calm inner radius, cross behind the planted megalith during reversal, and strike or bind the exposed wrist anchor before the chain lifts into the opposite orbit.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Hill Giants roll boulders into the outer orbit and Brutes sweep them loose, expanding the ring only while the Stone Giant maintains its anchor; breaking the wrist pivot returns those attacks to independent lanes.

monsters.name: Mountain Lord
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control multiple terrain routes by opening shoulder waterfalls, dropping pine-marked scree, and assigning lower Giants to exploit the dry route that remains.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read a living landscape as a command interface: water, pines, and ring-sized chains announce which route will flood, collapse, or remain safe before the Mountain Lord commits.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Three Watersheds: the Mountain Lord turns one gate-sized iron ring at its waist to open a shoulder fall, tilts a pine-crag to release scree across a second route, and points lower forms toward the third. The Lord must brace both arms against the terrain while changing the watershed, exposing a runed sternum shelf.
monsters.telegraph: Pines bend toward one back crag, one waterfall narrows to a suspended sheet, and the selected iron ring groans as both massive hands reach for the landscape.
monsters.counterplay: Follow the bending pines to the route that will stay dry, redirect a Hill Giant roll into the selected ring, or climb the grounded arm and strike the sternum rune while both hands manage the watershed.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Brutes sweep the newly dry route, Hill Giants roll along the drained channel, and Stone Giants anchor chains across flooded routes; breaking the selected ring makes those orders arrive as ordinary isolated attacks.

monsters.name: Primordial Titan
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Serve as the changing arena itself, carrying a valley that tilts through timber, slope, orbit, and watershed phases while lower Giants operate visible anchors across its back.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of every scale-reading lesson by asking players to identify the Titan's next weight shift, disable the lower-form crew shaping that phase, and move between stable landscape anchors before the valley changes orientation.
monsters.signatureMechanic: March of the Range: the battle occupies the valley on the Titan's back. At four gait beats, the Titan repeats the family grammar at landscape scale: a forested ridge falls like Timber Fall, a glacier rolls loose like Hill Roll, a chain of standing stones sweeps around a central peak like Megalith Orbit, and shoulder rivers reroute through Three Watersheds. A Brute, Hill Giant, Stone Giant, or Mountain Lord operates the matching rune anchor; disabling that crew and breaking its anchor removes the phase. After two anchors fall, the Titan kneels and rotates the valley ninety degrees, opening new paths through its beard glaciers rather than becoming a larger version of the Champion.
monsters.telegraph: Clouds shear at the waist, furnace-warm eyes narrow without casting an aura, one valley rune darkens, and the corresponding forest, glacier, standing-stone chain, or river system begins moving several beats before the Titan's foot lands.
monsters.counterplay: Use the announced landscape route to reach the active lower Giant, defeat or displace it, fracture the exposed rune anchor during the Titan's footfall recovery, and relocate to a surviving standing-stone shelter before the valley rotates; every destroyed anchor permanently removes one gait phase.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Each lower Giant operates the anchor that enlarges its learned mechanic, and the Titan's phase ends early when that operator is removed; surviving operators relocate when the valley rotates, preserving readable continuity across the boss encounter.

monsters.name: Scrag
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe close space with long-arm swipes while one visibly open gash cycles between collapse and rapid regrowth, creating a simple interrupt-or-withdraw decision.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the family's foundational regeneration rule: the dangerous recovery is announced by a pale wound bud, and striking that bud matters more than trading into already healed mass.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Bad Closure: after a committed swipe, one half-healing gash contracts into a pale bud that will restore the arm's next attack and seal some damage; interruption at the bud stops the closure and makes the arm hang slack for one cycle.
monsters.telegraph: The mud-caked Scrag hunches over one always-open gash, whose rim pales and draws inward while the long attacking hand goes limp.
monsters.counterplay: Step outside the preceding swipe, then strike the pale bud before the gash seals; missing that window lets the Scrag rebound immediately with the restored arm.

monsters.name: Bog Troll
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Apply repeatable pin pressure by using the rusted blade healed into its side as an anchor for a long-arm drag, then regenerate behind shoulder knots while the target is held.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that embedded debris is both a Troll weapon and a weak point: the rusted blade enables the pin, but moving or removing it interrupts the surrounding regrowth.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Bog Anchor: the Troll hooks a rope around the blade in its side and throws the loop with one long arm; if the loop catches, it braces against tumorous shoulder knots and drags the target toward the blade-side wound.
monsters.telegraph: The shoulder knots harden, one hand feeds muddy rope around the protruding blade, and the potbelly turns so the blade-side gash faces the target.
monsters.counterplay: Avoid the widening rope loop, cut it during the drag, or strike the rusted blade sideways to reopen the anchor wound and soften the braced shoulder.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: A Bog Troll drags targets into a Scrag's long reach and can stand between a healing Scrag and its wound bud; pulling the embedded blade forces the Soldier to abandon that cover.

monsters.name: Mutant Troll
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Change the encounter by presenting three incompatible regrowth paths—grasping arm, biting neck jaw, or rib barricade—and forcing the player to choose which mutation the Troll completes.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the qualitative Specialist pivot: Troll regeneration is now steerable encounter state, and reading which wound is fed allows the player to trade one known hazard for interrupting a worse one.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Wrong-Part Fork: after taking a knee, the Mutant pushes healing mass toward one of three visible buds. The shoulder bud completes an extra grappling arm, the neck seam opens the second jaw into a short denial cone, and the outward ribs knit into a stationary chest-high barrier. Striking the active bud cancels that mutation but diverts the remaining mass to the next clockwise bud, which completes faster; breaking the pale feeder scar stops the fork entirely.
monsters.telegraph: A thick pulse travels around the asymmetric torso, one bud turns pale and swells, and the extra arm, neck jaw, or outward ribs twitch before their distinct form locks in.
monsters.counterplay: Identify the active bud, decide whether its known zone is tolerable, and if not strike it before completion; after one diversion, cut the visibly stretched feeder scar rather than chasing every bud.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Bog Troll anchors can hold targets inside the jaw cone and Scrags shelter behind the rib barrier, but either lower form can also block the feeder scar and become leverage for interrupting the mutation path.

monsters.name: Scarlord
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Build temporary healing territory by tearing off overlapping chest plates as cover and regrowth beds, then using mismatched limbs to patrol the seams between them.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach space-control prioritization: the Scarlord's old scars make lower Trolls recover safely, but every shed plate exposes a fresh soft layer and creates a seam players can exploit.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Palimpsest Plates: the Scarlord peels one bark-hard chest plate and slams it into the bog. Trolls touching its wet inner face regenerate without exposing their usual bud, while the Scarlord loses armor at the matching chest quadrant. Two adjacent plates can overlap into a covered healing pocket, but striking their bright wet seam collapses both.
monsters.telegraph: Mismatched arms hook beneath a cracked chest plate, dark fluid beads around its edge, and nearby Trolls turn their open wounds toward the glistening inner surface.
monsters.counterplay: Attack the newly soft chest quadrant, strike the wet overlap before lower forms enter, or force the Scarlord to place plates apart so they cannot form a protected pocket.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Scrags close Bad Closure against a plate, Bog Trolls anchor enemies at its edge, and Mutant Trolls feed buds without exposing the feeder scar; destroying the plate restores every familiar interruption window.

monsters.name: Elder Troll
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Run a production-and-transformation boss encounter that reopens centuries of embedded injuries, buds new lower Trolls from those wounds, and absorbs surviving forms to author the next body phase.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of buds, lodged anchors, mutation forks, and scar seams by making every boss phase visibly originate from one embedded weapon or forming head that can be interrupted before its historical wound takes over the arena.
monsters.signatureMechanic: History Heals Wrong: weapons from a dozen armies divide the Elder's walking landscape into four wound beds. Pulling a spear opens a gash that buds two Scrags; wrenching a rusted sword produces a rope-wielding Bog Troll; feeding a half-formed head completes a Mutant Troll's chosen extra structure; shedding the oldest chest landscape creates a Scarlord healing plate. The Elder chooses one bed by turning its most awake head toward it, while lower Trolls may crawl back into an open bed to be absorbed and accelerate that phase. Permanently severing a bed's pale root scar removes its production option. After two roots fall, different forming heads take control of opposite mismatched limbs, creating alternating tells rather than a simple damage escalation.
monsters.telegraph: One head opens its eyes, nearby embedded weapons flex outward, and a pale root scar pulses from that head to the selected wound bed while incomplete faces along the route begin mouthing the lower form's tell.
monsters.counterplay: Interrupt retreating lower Trolls before absorption, use the selected embedded weapon as leverage to expose its root, sever that root during the production contraction, and reposition between the independently signaled limb attacks after the head-control phase begins.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: The Elder produces Scrags, Bog Trolls, and Mutant Troll structures from specific historical wounds, sheds Scarlord-grade terrain, and can absorb any surviving lower Troll to speed the matching phase; severed roots permanently end those exchanges.

monsters.name: Whelp
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe ground spacing by circling one claimed shiny object and making a committed four-legged pounce across its edge.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the Dragon family's territorial movement grammar before flight appears: read head, tail, and hind-leg loading, then use the claimed center against the attacker.
monsters.signatureMechanic: First Claim: the Whelp noses one loose hoard object into a visible circle and pounces at anything crossing the boundary; the oversized head pulls the landing forward, leaving the hornless nape and belly exposed until it scrambles around the claim again.
monsters.telegraph: Wet-looking scales tighten over the hind legs, the oversized head lowers beside the shiny claim, and the long tail goes rigid along the intended pounce line.
monsters.counterplay: Feint across one side of the circle and leave before launch, then cross behind the rigid tail and strike the exposed nape or pale belly during the clumsy landing.

monsters.name: Fledgling
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Apply repeatable short-range pressure by converting the Whelp's pounce into a low wing-assisted hop that can clear one obstacle but must land on a visible second claim.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach takeoff and landing as separate tells: immature wings extend reach but cannot correct midair, so the marked landing claim is the reliable counterplay anchor.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Claim Hop: the Fledgling bats a hoard object to mark its landing, beats its small membrane wings once, and glides on a fixed arc toward it; a bad landing folds one unreliable wing beneath the body before recovery.
monsters.telegraph: One clean horn pair points at the landing object, glossy scales lift over the deep chest, and both small wings stretch to their full but visibly trembling span.
monsters.counterplay: Move away from the marked object rather than tracking the body in flight, or displace the claim before landing to force the wing-fold recovery.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Whelps guard the landing claim and may pounce at players leaving it; drawing them across the fixed glide line makes the Fledgling abort or collide with its own screen.

monsters.name: Drake
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Transform the encounter into a three-dimensional lane hunt by drawing a complete aerial circuit, crossing it once at speed, and turning only around a readable horn-side pressure anchor.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the qualitative Specialist pivot: full wings create authored airspace rather than simple extra reach, and the safe response is to read the circuit and attack its inner turning anchor.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Crown Circuit: the Drake flies a broad loop that leaves three physical tells—claw-scraped launch stone, one shed spinal scale at the far turn, and a tail gouge at landing—then makes a fast pass through those points. Its broad wings can bank only toward the horn branch angled inside the loop, exposing that inner wing knuckle during the turn.
monsters.telegraph: The proper crown of horns tilts toward the inner circuit, the metallic spinal ridge rises to the tail tip, and one broad wing lowers as the three route markers align.
monsters.counterplay: Stand outside the aligned markers, move into the inner lee after the pass, and strike the lowered wing knuckle while the Drake banks around its fixed horn-side anchor.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Whelps contest the launch stone and Fledglings hop toward the landing gouge, but moving either claim out of alignment breaks the Drake's complete circuit and forces a grounded reset.

monsters.name: Elder Wyrm
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control takeoff and landing zones by unfurling scarred sun-blocking wings and shedding fused belly coins into temporary roost lines that organize younger Dragons' movement.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the Champion combines territory and flight: the gold-fall makes dangerous routes visible and useful to lower forms, while every torn membrane seam and recently emptied belly patch remains punishable.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Hoardfall Roost: the Elder Wyrm rakes one coin-fused belly plate across a scarred wing spar, releasing a line of hot, heavy coins between a launch perch and landing mound. Younger Dragons use the line as a shared claim and circuit edge; the Wyrm guards it with one sun-blot wing sweep but cannot cover the torn trailing membrane.
monsters.telegraph: Chipped horns lower, fused belly coins lift like scales, and sunlight appears through one old membrane tear as the massive wing stretches over the selected route.
monsters.counterplay: Cross through the visible membrane tear, scatter the coin line before lower Dragons establish claims, or strike the pale belly patch exposed where the fused hoard was shed.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Whelps claim individual coins, Fledglings use them as landing marks, and Drakes align circuits along the roost line; scattering that line dissolves all three movement benefits at once.

monsters.name: Dragon Emperor
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a phased territorial boss arena through four hoard-metal horizon pylons, each transforming the arena into one learned ground, hop, circuit, or roost grammar before the Emperor enters the exposed center.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of claimed centers, fixed landings, inner flight anchors, and hoardfall routes by asking players to break the pylon supporting each phase while managing the corresponding lower Dragons.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Imperial Circuit: four hoard-metal pylons face the arena horizons beneath the Emperor's storm-front wings. The Claw pylon causes Whelps to establish moving claims; the Wing pylon links Fledgling landing marks; the Crown pylon closes a Drake circuit; and the Hoard pylon lets an Elder Wyrm lay a coin roost. The Emperor branches its antler crown toward one pylon, conducts that lower-form phase, then lands on the central hoard with one body-warm heat shimmer and grows the selected pylon's metal across the matching armor quadrant. Breaking a pylon during the landing permanently removes both command and armor growth. After two breaks, the Emperor alternates ground and sky sides of the arena through the surviving grammar instead of repeating the Elder Wyrm at larger scale.
monsters.telegraph: One antler branch hooks toward a horizon, the matching hoard metal rings through the hide, the vast wings bank like a storm front, and every lower Dragon turns its head, horn, or landing marker toward the selected pylon.
monsters.counterplay: Follow the selected lower-form tell, disrupt its claims or route, attack the pylon when the Emperor commits to the central landing, and use the opened armor quadrant as shelter from the alternating ground-sky pass; each destroyed pylon permanently simplifies the circuit.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Whelps, Fledglings, Drakes, and an Elder Wyrm each operate one pylon's learned territorial grammar; destroying that pylon removes the relevant command, route benefit, and armor quadrant for the rest of the fight.

monsters.name: Rattler
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe target selection with brittle shortsword pressure, then turn one strong hit into a short reassembly puzzle centered on the loose skull.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the family's binding rule: scattering the body creates safety only temporarily, while disabling the dim socket anchor prevents the bones from rattling back together.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Loose Muster: a strong interruption scatters the Rattler into a skull, ribcage, and limb piles; dull socket pinpoints travel down visible rune scratches and pull the nearest pieces back unless the skull is displaced or struck before the ribs stand.
