monsters.telegraph: Gap teeth chatter, the frame visibly loosens at every joint, and the dull socket pinpoints draw thin lines toward the nearest dropped bones.
monsters.counterplay: Scatter it away from other bone piles, then kick or strike the skull before the ribcage rises; destroying ordinary limb fragments alone only delays the same reassembly.

monsters.name: Bonesoldier
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Hold a repeatable narrow front by tensioning rusted mail between spine and forearm shield, protecting loose skeletons while exposing the strapped arm after a committed block.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that stronger binding is equipment-mediated: read which mail section carries the load, then break or bypass it rather than striking the shielded bone mass.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Grave-Line Brace: the Bonesoldier twists its torso until rusted mail pulls taut from spine to shield forearm, catching one frontal attack and keeping adjacent Rattler bones inside its binding shadow; the twist leaves the sword shoulder open and the shield strap fully loaded.
monsters.telegraph: Weak ember light passes from the sockets into one mail row, the strapped shield turns edge-on, and the spine rotates until the corroded links sing under tension.
monsters.counterplay: Attack from the open sword-shoulder side, cut the bright loaded mail row, or displace the forearm shield so the strap tears when the torso completes its twist.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Rattler fragments inside the shield-side binding shadow reform faster and cannot be kicked outward, but cutting the loaded mail scatters both the Soldier and any half-raised Rattler pile it covers.

monsters.name: Bone Knight
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Change the encounter economy by claiming scattered bones from either side of the battlefield, forging them into one temporary intercepting limb, lance, or plated-rib barrier.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the qualitative Specialist pivot: loose bones are now a contested resource, and controlling the visible levy route matters more than attacking the Knight's thickened frame head-on.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Bone Levy: the fused helm marks one loose bone pile with a socket-fire line, and the plated ribcage opens to receive it. Arm bones produce a long intercepting lance, ribs produce a forward cage barrier, and skulls produce a second lookout mounted on the shoulder. Only one levy can be active; striking the moving pile or the bright rib seam before it locks denies the construction and leaves the chest open.
monsters.telegraph: The bright socket flame narrows toward one bone pile, the helm turns without the shoulders, and the plated ribcage spreads along a clearly lit central seam.
monsters.counterplay: Move or destroy the marked pile, cross the light line before the fragments reach the chest, or strike the bright rib seam during intake; once built, attack from the side the chosen bone structure cannot cover.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: The Knight can levy a scattered Rattler or broken Bonesoldier into its chosen structure, preventing that lower form from reassembling; denying the levy leaves those bones available to disrupt or bait later pulls.

monsters.name: Bone Champion
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Fuse scattered remains into crown-shaped barricades that extend shield lines, define levy channels, and command lower skeletons through a deliberately breakable arena formation.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach formation dismantling: the Champion's fused mass is least vulnerable at the center, while every new spur wall creates an outer binding seam that can collapse the whole structure.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Crownwork: the Champion plants one shoulder spur, draws loose bones into a curving wall, and completes it with the opposite spur to form a crown point. Bonesoldiers lock shields into the wall, Bone Knights levy through its interior channel, and Rattlers reform behind it. The Champion must keep one horned side turned toward each completed point, exposing the unfused hip seam on the opposite side.
monsters.telegraph: Shoulder spurs rise like crown tines, one horn on the skull aligns with a bone pile, and a bright binding line traces the planned curve across the floor before fragments move.
monsters.counterplay: Cross the planned curve before it closes, break the outermost shoulder-spur seam, or attack the hip opposite the Champion's turned horn; one broken crown point opens every lower-form route attached to it.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Rattlers reform behind crownwork, Bonesoldiers extend it with shield braces, and Bone Knights draw levy fragments through it; breaking one spur point removes protection and interrupts every attached interaction.

monsters.name: Lich King
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a four-seal boss court that reassembles, equips, levies, and fuses lower skeletons while the royal halo changes orbit to expose one production gap at a time.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of skull anchors, loaded mail, levy routes, and crown seams by making players interrupt the exact grave seal producing each learned formation before the King can bind it into the next rank.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Royal Ossuary: four independent grave-seal paths surround the throne—the Rattle seal assembles loose bones as Rattlers, the Mail seal equips a separate bone levy as Bonesoldiers, the Helm seal raises armored remains as Bone Knights, and the Crown seal fuses its own guarded ossuary into a Bone Champion. Each path produces or promotes its source-supported form without requiring the previous tier's promotion. The Lich King points its staff of bound souls at one seal, and the halo of orbiting fragments opens a matching gap to feed it. Destroying the exposed seal permanently removes that path and leaves a wider halo gap. After two seals fall, the King descends from the throne and wears the remaining halo fragments as asymmetrical skeletal limbs, cycling their familiar mechanics instead of merely enlarging the Champion.
monsters.telegraph: The jeweled crown inclines toward one grave seal, souls pull visibly down the staff, and the slow bone halo opens over that same route while lower skeletons turn their socket-fire toward it.
monsters.counterplay: Follow the halo gap, scatter or intercept the lower form designated for promotion, strike the exposed seal before the staff pulse completes, and use each permanent gap to approach the King during the dismounted phase.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Independent Rattle, Mail, Helm, and Crown paths produce or promote Rattlers, Bonesoldiers, Bone Knights, and Bone Champions from their own remains without requiring a previous-tier promotion; every destroyed seal permanently removes one production or transformation rule and expands the King's exposed halo gap.

monsters.name: Shambler
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe spacing with an uneven advance whose dragging foot stores one sudden fall-lunge along the line of the corpse's visible death wound.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that apparent slowness is a readable load cycle: identify the dragging side, leave its fall lane, and punish the exposed ankle before the corpse hauls itself upright.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Last Step: grave dirt gathers under the dragging foot until the Shambler's wrong-angled head snaps toward a target; it releases the stored imbalance as a full-body fall and clawing slide, then must pull the dislocated shoulder and ankle back under itself.
monsters.telegraph: The dragging heel stops, strips of funeral clothing pull taut toward the planted leg, and the hanging jaw closes once before the whole corpse tips.
monsters.counterplay: Step across the healthy-leg side rather than retreating down the fall lane, then strike or displace the exposed dragging ankle while the Shambler reconstructs its stance.

monsters.name: Ghoul
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Apply reliable pursuit by hooking one claw into terrain or a fallen body and using exposed arm sinew to slingshot through a short, fixed chase lane.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the mature rot grammar: faster movement is built from visible tendon tension, so cutting the anchor line or crossing behind the hooked hand defeats the rush.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Carrion Draw: the Ghoul plants a hooked hand, cords the exposed sinew along both arms, and reels its fresher body into a jaw-first rush; a Shambler lying in the lane becomes an optional anchor that lengthens the pull but does not change its direction.
monsters.telegraph: One claw bites into floor, wall, or corpse, the arm sinew rises like cables, and the clenched jaw points straight down the chosen lane.
monsters.counterplay: Break or displace the hooked hand, cross behind the planted shoulder, or interrupt the exposed tendon before the body releases; the Ghoul overshoots if its anchor vanishes late.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: A fallen or recovering Shambler can serve as a longer Carrion Draw anchor; moving the Shambler changes or shortens the Ghoul's fixed rush without empowering the Shambler itself.

monsters.name: Rot Brute
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the floor into route control by pumping infected matter through existing corpse trails, turning familiar Shambler falls and Ghoul anchors into timed eruption lines.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read an arena network rather than only a body: sever a marked trail, jam the open rib pump, or use a clean lane before the Brute pressurizes it.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Ribcage Peristalsis: the bloated Brute plants both forearm bone blades and opens its cracked ribs like pump handles. One visible wet trail leading to a Shambler or Ghoul pulses from corpse to corpse, then erupts in a sequence of short grasping hands. Only one network can be charged; breaking any bright tendon junction stops the eruption and vents the Brute's belly.
monsters.telegraph: Forearm blades lock into the ground, the cracked ribcage spreads around a swollen central sac, and one chain of wet footprints and corpse seams begins pulsing toward the selected lane.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the pulsing route, sever one exposed tendon junction between bodies, or strike the swollen sac through the open ribs before the third pulse; the planted blades prevent the Brute from turning during the cast.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Shambler fall lanes and Ghoul anchor routes become links in the chosen pump network; disrupting either lower form breaks that link and shortens the eruption instead of merely damaging the Brute.

monsters.name: Amalgam
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Rebuild the arena's movement lanes by assigning different fused torsos and extra arms to pull, brace, carry, or redirect lower Rotwalkers around its hulking mass.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach composite dismantling: the Amalgam is not one health sponge, because each visible corpse suture carries one duty and cutting it removes a specific lane or support action.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Borrowed Gaits: three folded heads call in sequence while their attached torsos act. The dragging torso sweeps a Shambler into a new fall lane, the hooked torso catches a Ghoul anchor, and the open-rib torso relays a Rot Brute pulse through the Amalgam. Each action loads a different stitched waist seam, and a severed seam permanently removes that gait.
monsters.telegraph: One folded head lifts and bites its own stitching, the matching pair of extra arms spreads, and a wet load line becomes visible from that torso to its lower-form partner.
monsters.counterplay: Identify the raised head, avoid its inherited lane, then attack the matching loaded waist suture; every severed torso reduces the Amalgam's command sequence and leaves an unguarded side.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Separate torsos reposition Shamblers, complete Ghoul anchor lines, and relay Rot Brute pumps; severing the responsible torso removes only that interaction for the rest of the encounter.

monsters.name: Plague Lord
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Rule a stitched-shroud boss arena that produces lower Rotwalkers, routes their death trails through four corpse aisles, and progressively transforms its throne into a mobile but mechanically simpler central body.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of dragging-side falls, tendon anchors, rib pumps, and loaded composite sutures by asking players to disable the exact corpse aisle supporting each command before confronting the released central face.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Throne of the Dead: four stitched-shroud aisles radiate from the Lord's fused-body throne. The Foot aisle assembles a Shambler and stores a fall lane; the Hand aisle cords a surviving corpse into a Ghoul; the Rib aisle pressurizes all connected trails through a Rot Brute; and the Many aisle folds two disabled bodies into an Amalgam. The central grinning face exhales a fly column toward one aisle while its corpses tighten that aisle's great suture. Cutting the exposed suture permanently collapses that production and tears one structural body from the throne. After two aisles fall, the remaining corpses unfold as mismatched limbs around the central body, which cycles only surviving commands and loses one limb whenever its matching aisle is destroyed.
monsters.telegraph: The stitched shrouds lift toward one aisle, flies stream in a single readable column, the central grin turns to the matching corpse arch, and its great wet suture pulls taut before bodies begin moving.
monsters.counterplay: Follow the fly column, interrupt or displace the lower form feeding the selected aisle, cut the taut great suture during production, and use each collapsed aisle as clean ground; every destroyed aisle permanently removes a command, a throne support, and one later transformation limb.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: The four aisles produce or promote Shamblers, Ghouls, Rot Brutes, and Amalgams and route their learned mechanics; destroying an aisle removes its lower-form production and the corresponding command from every later phase.

monsters.name: Shade
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe recognition by fading to a low smear of vapor, then condensing around two cold eye points for one short life-draining reach.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the eyes are both warning and anchor: the Shade can be harmed only as the second point steadies and its humanoid outline becomes readable.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Held Look: one cold point fixes on a target while the second drifts through the fog; when the two align, a faint shoulder-and-hand outline condenses for a single touch before smearing away again.
monsters.telegraph: The wandering point slows, the two lights level like eyes, and nearby vapor draws inward to sketch one raised shoulder and hand.
monsters.counterplay: Move across the drifting point to delay alignment, then strike between the two lights during the brief complete outline rather than attacking the surrounding fog.

monsters.name: Haunt
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat spectral condensation as dependable lane pressure by dragging a rusted chain through a wall or obstacle and making the chain's exit point the Haunt's next attack threshold.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that incorporeal movement still owes a material anchor: follow the chain, avoid its selected threshold, and pull or strike it while the Haunt emerges.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Funeral Drag: the Haunt casts its dragging chain through one nearby surface; the hood and skeletal-suggested hands dissolve, then re-form at the chain's far hook for a sweeping touch while the lower body remains vapor.
monsters.telegraph: Trailing tatters stream toward the wall, the chain hook scrapes a bright line through it, and the hood turns toward the unseen exit before dissolving.
monsters.counterplay: Read the hook's scrape line, leave the exit threshold, and pull or strike the taut chain during emergence; breaking tension strands the Haunt half-defined beside the surface.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: A Shade may condense around the Haunt's far hook, revealing the exit earlier but adding a second touch threat; disrupting the chain also scatters that Shade's alignment.

monsters.name: Wraith
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the floor into boundary prediction by orbiting several chains around a fully defined spectral blade and choosing one contacted surface as the blade's remote emergence edge.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to watch the moving chain orbit, identify which surface it has claimed, and attack the exposed blade hilt while the striking edge exists elsewhere.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Borrowed Edge: three orbiting chains sweep the room until one link touches a wall, pillar, or shield. The Wraith passes only the spectral blade through that marked boundary, causing its edge to emerge along the entire touched line while the robed body and hilt remain fixed. Severing the contacting chain or striking the hilt collapses the remote edge.
monsters.telegraph: The visible skeletal hands reverse their grip, one orbiting chain stops against a surface, and cold light runs from the fixed link through the blade hilt before the remote edge appears.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the marked boundary, sever the motionless contacting link, or close on the stationary hilt while the blade is committed elsewhere; the other two chains continue orbiting but cannot strike.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Haunts can route their Funeral Drag along the claimed boundary and Shades condense at its corners; breaking the fixed Wraith chain interrupts those routes as well as the remote blade.

monsters.name: Crowned Specter
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Spread a cloak-shaped territory across the arena, assigning its hem, folds, and crown points as condensation, chain, and remote-edge routes for lower Wraiths.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach territorial dismantling: the black tide is a mapped cloak rather than generic darkness, and breaking the crown point holding one fold permanently opens that region.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Crown-Tide: three spectral crown points pin the widening cloak to floor and walls. One fold aligns Shade eyes, one carries Haunt chains, and one lets a Wraith borrow its hem as an edge. The Specter must face the active fold, leaving the opposite crown point rimmed in family-native frost and materially condensed.
monsters.telegraph: The faceless hood turns, one crown point lowers, and a single cloak fold spreads outward as frost traces its hem and lower spirits drift toward it.
monsters.counterplay: Move off the traced hem, attack the opposite frost-rimmed crown point, and use the opened tear as clear ground; each broken point permanently removes its assigned lower-form route.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Separate cloak folds accelerate Shade alignment, extend Haunt chain thresholds, and supply Wraith remote edges; breaking a crown point disables the linked fold for every spirit.

monsters.name: Death Sovereign
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a four-seal funeral court from hollow armor, composing alignment, threshold, borrowed-edge, and black-tide phases before abandoning broken regalia for a simpler exposed void form.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of every spectral anchor by having players follow a learnable court procession, break the armor seal funding its command, and permanently simplify both arena and boss.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Last Court: four ornate armor seals ring the Sovereign's empty cuirass and align to funeral arches around the arena. The Eye seal calls Shades to align across one arch; the Chain seal sends Haunts through paired thresholds; the Blade seal gives a Wraith a remote scythe edge; and the Crown seal spreads a Crowned Specter's cloak between arches. The Sovereign lifts its frozen-smoke scythe toward one seal while a court of lesser shades forms a procession to the matching arch. Striking the exposed seal during that command shatters its arch and removes the phase. After two seals break, the hollow armor opens and the void wears the surviving plates as two asymmetric anchors, cycling only surviving commands with shorter, clearer routes.
monsters.telegraph: One armor seal turns toward the viewer, the scythe condenses along that seal's arch, stars in the night-sky robe stop moving, and the lesser-shade court forms a single-file route to the selected station.
monsters.counterplay: Read the procession and familiar lower-form tell, move away from the chosen arch, then strike the outward-facing armor seal while the scythe is committed; each shattered seal removes one command, one arena arch, and one plate from the void phase.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Shades, Haunts, Wraiths, and a Crowned Specter each operate one court seal and funeral arch; destroying that seal dismisses its lower-form procession and prevents the Sovereign from repeating its grammar.

monsters.name: Thrall
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe wound awareness with a feral crawl that follows one visible blood scent, commits both clawed hands to a pounce, and becomes vulnerable while feeding.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the family bargain early: a Vampire gains tempo only from a readable wound or vessel, and denying the feed leaves its throat and back exposed.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Red Trail: the Thrall lowers its rat-like face to a fresh blood mark, scrambles along that fixed scent line, and tackles at the end; if it reaches the mark, it feeds for one beat to ready another rush.
monsters.telegraph: Red eyes drop to the floor, filthy shoulders bunch above the ears, and both clawed hands spread while the nose tracks one visible line.
monsters.counterplay: Step across rather than along the scent line, cover or move away from the marked wound, then punish the exposed neck and spine during the committed feed.

monsters.name: Bloodkin
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Apply repeatable hunting pressure by pinning a blood mark beneath one coat hem, circling with long claws, then snapping into a fixed inward rake.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that refinement means controlled predation: watch which hem is planted, exit on the unweighted side, and attack the overextended claw rather than fleeing the circle.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Hunter's Hem: the Bloodkin steps one dark coat tail onto a blood mark and circles it at arm's length; when slicked-back hair and coat align, the hunter cuts inward with both claws but cannot reverse around the pinned hem.
monsters.telegraph: One boot and coat tail stop over the red mark, long claws lower to hip height, and the still-hunched shoulders square toward the circle's center.
monsters.counterplay: Cross behind the pinned coat tail, pull the fight off the blood mark, or strike the weighted boot during the inward rake; the Bloodkin must release the hem before pursuing again.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Thralls follow the Bloodkin's circular blood scent but collide with its committed inward rake if baited across the pinned hem, turning the shared mark into counterplay.

monsters.name: Noble
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the encounter into a formal duel by offering one target a blood-glass crest and enforcing a readable lane of courtesy while other attacks empower the crest.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to accept or deliberately break a social-looking combat rule: face the Noble inside the offered lane, shatter the vessel during its bow, and never feed the crest with stray hits.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Red Courtesy: the composed Noble cuts one drop from its glove into a blood-glass crest at the cane tip and bows toward a target. A narrow velvet-red lane forms between them. The Noble may thrust only along that lane, but attacks entering from outside are caught by the crest and returned as one widening slash. Striking the extended cane hand during the bow shatters the crest and ends the duel.
monsters.telegraph: One glove is drawn off finger by finger, the cane or ornate blade turns flat beneath a falling blood drop, and the Noble bows without breaking red-eyed contact.
monsters.counterplay: Either stay in the visible lane and sidestep the fixed thrust, or commit to breaking the duel by striking the extended cane hand during the bow; do not fire through the crest from outside.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Thralls and Bloodkin are held outside the courtesy lane but chase anyone who leaves it; shattering the crest releases them without granting the Noble a reflected slash.

monsters.name: Ancient
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control several duel spaces by opening sections of a bat-membrane cloak with ringed fingers, screening hunters and redirecting blood-glass lanes through deliberate salon geometry.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach command-hand prioritization: each signet controls one cloak panel and inherited rule, and attacking the loaded finger permanently tears that panel from the formation.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Century Salon: the Ancient extends one ringed finger to tension a matching cloak rib. The Fang panel releases Thralls down a scent lane, the Hem panel curves a Bloodkin circle, and the Crest panel bends a Noble courtesy lane around the cloak. The active signet cannot close until the command resolves, leaving its finger and membrane joint exposed.
monsters.telegraph: The perfectly still face turns by a fraction, one ornate signet catches the available light, and the matching bat-membrane panel stretches between arm and cloak like a dark room divider.
monsters.counterplay: Read the bright signet, avoid the familiar rule within its panel, and strike either the extended finger or taut membrane joint; a torn panel removes that command and opens the salon sightline.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Distinct cloak panels route Thrall scent rushes, Bloodkin circles, and Noble duel lanes; destroying a panel removes its lower-form command for the encounter.

monsters.name: Progenitor
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Rule a three-crest blood-glass throne arena that stages Hunt, Courtesy, and Salon phases, promotes surviving lower Vampires, and sheds one shadow-wing command each time its lineage vessel breaks.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of scent lines, pinned hems, duel crests, and command panels while giving every destroyed lineage vessel a permanent, visible simplification of the boss and arena.
monsters.signatureMechanic: First Blood Court: three tall blood-glass vessels rise behind the throne beneath the grown-looking crown. The Hunt vessel marks wounds and sends Thralls that surviving Bloodkin can pull into circles; the Courtesy vessel appoints a Noble whose shattered crest opens a strike on the throne; the Salon vessel lets an Ancient divide the arena with cloak panels. The Progenitor spreads one pure-shadow wing toward the selected vessel and feeds it through a visible glass vein. Breaking that vein during the lower-form phase shatters the vessel, dismisses its command, and tears away the corresponding wing section. Once two vessels fall, the Progenitor leaves the throne, using only the remaining crest while each shadow-wing recovery exposes the crown root.
monsters.telegraph: The impossibly still face turns toward one vessel, a fine crown branch aligns with its glass vein, the matching shadow wing unfolds, and every lower Vampire adopts that phase's learned posture.
monsters.counterplay: Follow the selected crest, resolve or disrupt its familiar lower-form rule, then sever the visible throne vein while the wing is extended; every broken vessel removes a phase, a command route, and one protective wing section.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: The three vessels command and promote Thralls, Bloodkin, Nobles, and an Ancient through Hunt, Courtesy, and Salon grammar; destroying a vessel ends its promotions and prevents the Progenitor from using that grammar again.

monsters.name: Husk
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe footwork by dragging one crude wrapping end behind a stiff advance, then pulling the strip into a short ankle snare before the exposed knot can be retied.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that linen is both animation and weakness: avoid the visible strip, step on it after the pull, and attack the knot while dried flesh shows through the loosened gap.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Common-Grave Draw: the Husk advances on one dragging leg while a gray bandage end trails from its hip; when the arms lift, the end loops around the nearest ankle line and retracts toward the hip knot.
monsters.telegraph: Empty eye holes face down, both stiff arms rise, and the dirty trailing strip straightens from the dragging leg to its hip knot.
monsters.counterplay: Step over or pin the strip before it retracts, then cut the visible hip knot; the Husk must stop and rewrap the gap before it can snare again.

monsters.name: Tomb Guard
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Hold a repeatable doorway or relic line by crossing khopesh and wrapped forearm, transferring the block through a row of bronze charms that leaves one stitch overloaded.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach mature binding: do not batter the dry front; draw the committed guard, read which charm row tightens, and cut the last loaded stitch from the side.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Tomb Cross: the Guard crosses its bronze khopesh over one wrapped forearm and turns sideways across a threshold. Bronze charms stitched from wrist to shoulder carry the impact, but the topmost charm pulls one linen seam fully open after the block.
monsters.telegraph: The simple headcloth settles, khopesh and forearm cross, and bronze charms click in order from wrist toward shoulder until the final stitch shines.
monsters.counterplay: Bait the cross with a light attack, move around the weapon side, and cut the final shoulder stitch before the charm row relaxes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Husks can drag loose ends behind the guarded threshold, but breaking the Tomb Cross's final stitch opens the line and tears any Husk strip caught beneath its stance.

monsters.name: Sacred Servant
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the encounter into ordered route control by unspooling three gilded glyph bands that record movement and then rewind along the same processional sequence.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read glyph order, deliberately cross one strip to create an escape break, and interrupt the collar clasp before the recorded path pulls combatants backward.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Written Procession: the Servant extends three gilded bands from its jeweled collar, touching floor points in a clearly numbered glyph order. After the third point, the bands tighten in reverse and drag anyone standing on a recorded segment back toward the previous point. Crossing two bands before completion tangles them; striking the open collar clasp cancels the rewind.
monsters.telegraph: The jeweled collar opens at one front clasp, faint family-native glyph light travels one-two-three along separate bands, and the Servant's stiff hands cross before the order reverses.
monsters.counterplay: Track the numbered glow, leave the latest segment, cross two loose bands to tangle them, or strike the exposed collar clasp before the hands complete their cross.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Husks and Tomb Guards are pulled backward along the same recorded sequence to renew snares or thresholds; tangling the bands displaces those lower forms and interrupts every rewind.

monsters.name: Pharaoh's Champion
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Assemble lower Mummies into a four-sided tomb formation by turning its gold death-mask toward one side and directing native sand only as a readable footprint record.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach formation rotation: the mask faces the protected side, the rear strap and ceremonial armor seam carry its weight, and breaking that seam permanently removes one formation wall.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Four-Faced Tomb: the Champion's full death-mask turns toward a cardinal side while ceremonial armor plates unfold along that edge. Husks trail snare strips across one flank, Tomb Guards cross the front, and a Sacred Servant writes a return path behind. Sand disturbed at their feet records every occupied line but has no independent elemental force. The opposite mask strap stretches visibly under the formation load.
monsters.telegraph: The gold mask rotates with a dry click, one armor edge opens, native sand swirls only around moving feet, and the opposite linen strap pulls away from the wrapped skull.
monsters.counterplay: Move through the side before the armor edge closes, avoid the familiar lower-form lines, and cut the rear mask strap; each broken strap prevents the Champion from rebuilding that side.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Husks supply snare flanks, Tomb Guards hold the faced edge, and Sacred Servants inscribe the rear return route; breaking the corresponding mask strap opens all three duties on that side.

monsters.name: God-King
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a royal tomb boss through a floating sarcophagus lid and four cartouche rails that bind, guard, rewind, and form lower Mummies before each broken rail simplifies the arena and final wrapped body.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of loose knots, loaded charm stitches, glyph order, and mask formations while teaching that the source title does not imply invulnerability: every royal command depends on a breakable material seal.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Royal Passage: the sarcophagus lid floats behind the God-King like a banner on four linen-and-gold rails. The Knot cartouche pulls Husks from common-grave alcoves; the Bronze cartouche equips survivors as Tomb Guards; the Script cartouche lets a Sacred Servant record a three-point procession; and the Mask cartouche closes a Pharaoh's Champion formation. The towering headdress points to one cartouche while family-native sand follows the moving rail, never acting independently. Cutting the lit cartouche's linen hinge permanently drops that lid quarter and removes its command. After two quarters fall, the God-King steps out of the remaining frame; its headdress shortens with each lost rail and it cycles only surviving rites around exposed wrapping knots.
monsters.telegraph: One lapis headdress vane aligns with a cartouche, its gold glyph becomes faintly readable, the matching lid rail swings forward, and lower Mummies cross their arms in the selected learned posture.
monsters.counterplay: Read the named cartouche and lower-form tell, disrupt the required Mummy or route, then cut the exposed linen hinge while the rail is forward; every dropped lid quarter removes one rite, clears an arena lane, and exposes another royal wrapping knot.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: The four cartouches produce or command Husks, Tomb Guards, Sacred Servants, and a Pharaoh's Champion; each severed hinge permanently ends that lower-form rite and simplifies the God-King's remaining phase.

monsters.name: Imp
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe target awareness by fluttering behind a marked combatant, stealing one visible infernal brand token with its tail, and becoming bolder only while carrying it.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that infernal power is routed through hierarchy marks: deny the theft, strike the tail-held token, and turn the Imp's tiny rank against higher forms.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Petty Theft: the Imp's whip tail hooks a loose brand shed by another Demon's attack or a marked arena object; while carrying it, the cat-sized pest can make one needle-tooth dive, but the token swings visibly behind and drops on any interruption.
monsters.telegraph: Pinprick horns angle back, small bat wings flutter in place, and the whip-thin tail circles one dark-red brand before darting for it.
monsters.counterplay: Move between the Imp and brand, hit the swinging tail during its straight dive, or collect the dropped token before another Demon can use it.

monsters.name: Fiend
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Apply reliable line pressure by stamping a stolen or self-shed brand beneath one goat-like hoof, then charging exactly along the brand's scorched direction.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the repeatable hierarchy grammar: the brand defines direction and fuel, so dislodging it or crossing behind the planted hoof defeats the charge.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Infernal Stamp: the Fiend presses one hoof onto a brand, opening source-native ember cracks from ankle to shoulder; it releases into a horn-first charge along the sigil's longest line and cannot steer after the hoof lifts.
monsters.telegraph: One curled horn lowers, the branded hoof grinds until its line is readable, and ember cracks open in sequence up the planted leg.
monsters.counterplay: Kick or strike the brand before release, cross the trailing-hoof side, or bait the fixed charge past cover; the ember cracks dim while the Fiend returns to the sigil.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Imps can deliver stolen brands to a Fiend for immediate stamping; interrupting the carrier denies the Fiend a charge rather than merely delaying the Imp.

monsters.name: Hellknight
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the floor into positional sentencing by locking one black plate seal and target brand together, forcing a visible choice between a narrow duel cell and breaking the armor route.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that a Specialist's authority has machinery: identify the selected horn pair, avoid crossing the branded boundary, and strike the opened plate seal while the flaming blade enforces elsewhere.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Sentence Brand: one pair of the Hellknight's four horns aligns with a chest-plate seal, casting a square brand around a target. The source-native flaming blade sweeps only the square's boundary, while the Hellknight must keep the selected seal open to sustain it. Crossing the line triggers the sweep; striking the open seal or forcing the Knight to turn beyond the aligned horns ends the sentence.
monsters.telegraph: Two horns lower into parallel lines, molten veins converge beneath one black spiked plate, and the flaming blade traces the square once before becoming active.
monsters.counterplay: Stay inside and evade the Knight's slower body, or attack through the unguarded open plate seal; alternatively force a turn that breaks the selected horn alignment before crossing the boundary.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Imps carry brands to the square corners and Fiends charge along one edge, but breaking the Hellknight's open seal erases every corner and interrupts any edge charge.

monsters.name: Archfiend
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Link brands, charge lines, and sentence cells into a command formation through separate bound-soul chains, each attached to one breakable fused-armor ring.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach hierarchy dismantling: each chain empowers one lower duty, but following its loaded arc reveals the exact armor ring whose destruction permanently removes that command.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Black Chain of Office: the Archfiend's crown of horns selects one of three soul chains. The Pest chain transfers stolen brands, the Charge chain links Fiend stamp lines, and the Sentence chain lets a Hellknight move its square once. Wings of source-native black smoke spread only to screen the active chain. Its fused obsidian armor ring opens under load.
monsters.telegraph: One horn-crown branch hooks downward, a single soul chain straightens toward its lower form, black-smoke wings part around that route, and the matching armor ring opens.
monsters.counterplay: Trace the taut chain past the smoke screen, resolve the familiar lower-form tell, and strike the opened armor ring; each broken ring dismisses its soul chain and simplifies the formation.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: The three chains coordinate Imp brand delivery, Fiend charge lines, and Hellknight sentence cells; breaking a chain ring removes that hierarchy benefit for all linked Demons.

monsters.name: Demon Prince
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command and promote an infernal legion from a source-native magma throne through four hierarchy brands, then tear free as a simpler winged body as destroyed throne channels strip commands and horn branches.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of brand theft, stamped lines, sentence seals, and soul-chain rings while making each interrupted promotion permanently remove part of the Prince's authority and final-phase silhouette.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Legion Crucible: four black-iron channels cross the magma throne beneath the Prince's branching horn corona. The Tail brand produces Imps from coal cages; the Hoof brand spends a delivered token to raise a Fiend; the Plate brand promotes a Fiend inside a sentence square into a Hellknight; and the Chain brand binds surviving elites under an Archfiend. The Prince points one corona branch to a channel, and its body becomes more native fire only along that visible route. Breaking the exposed brand plate during production drains the channel, removes that rank command, and snaps off the matching horn branch. After two breaks, the Prince leaves the throne with hide and joints reasserted around surviving native fire, cycling only remaining commands; each further plate destroys one wing-span brace and shortens the phase.
monsters.telegraph: One corona branch lowers toward a throne channel, source-native magma recedes to reveal its brand plate, the corresponding legion rank kneels or assembles, and the vast wings frame that single route.
monsters.counterplay: Read the selected rank and familiar lower-form tell, interrupt its required carrier or promotion, then strike the exposed throne plate before magma returns; each broken channel permanently removes a command, corona branch, and final-phase brace.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: The throne produces Imps, spends their brands on Fiends, promotes Fiends through Hellknight seals, and binds elites under an Archfiend; destroying a brand plate ends that production or promotion step for the fight.

monsters.name: Messenger
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe positional reading by delivering one straight ribbon decree between its simple halo and a marked floor point, then descending along that line with bare feet exposed.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that ordered actions are exact and interruptible: leave the announced line, then cut the ribbon seal or strike the dim halo joint during descent.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Single Word: the Messenger unrolls one ivory ribbon from the simple ring halo to a chosen point; sacred script advances once along it, and the slight two-wing figure descends in a straight line to deliver a palm strike before returning upward.
monsters.telegraph: Both soft wings fold evenly, the plain robe hangs still, and one readable script line travels from the simple halo down the taut ribbon.
monsters.counterplay: Step off the exact ribbon line and strike its floor seal or the dim ring joint while the Messenger's bare feet and folded wings are committed to descent.

monsters.name: Guardian
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Hold a repeatable luminous line by aligning round shield, spear, full two-wing span, and solid ring halo, then thrust only after the formation locks.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach mature order as geometry rather than toughness: force the shield off its halo diameter and punish the exposed rear wing root during the fixed thrust.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Golden Diameter: the Guardian places shield and spear on opposite ends of its solid halo's projected line. The two full wings brace symmetrically and the spear thrusts down that diameter; rotation is impossible until the shield grip releases.
monsters.telegraph: Gold plate settles, the round shield centers on one side of the halo, the spear tip reaches the opposite side, and both wing roots lock at equal angles.
monsters.counterplay: Move across the diameter rather than away from the spear, displace the shield grip, or strike the rear wing root while the thrust and opposite wing remain fixed.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Messenger ribbons can terminate at the Guardian's shield and borrow its diameter, but moving the shield breaks the message line and the brace together.

monsters.name: Warden
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the floor into intersecting-axis control by rotating two halo rings with separate wing pairs, creating one forbidden crossing and one deliberately safe quadrant.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read coupled geometry: match each wing pair to its ring, enter the quadrant where scripts disagree, and strike the stalled bearing before the axes realign.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Double Injunction: the upper wing pair rotates the outer halo ring and a line of script clockwise; the lower pair rotates the inner ring counterclockwise. Their projected axes sweep the arena, and where matching script meets becomes a damaging lock. Where unlike glyphs cross, both rings stall and reveal the central gold bearing as a safe attack window.
monsters.telegraph: Four wings separate into upper and lower pairs, two halo rings turn in opposite directions, and script drifts from the arms to mark both projected axes before they move.
monsters.counterplay: Track unlike glyphs rather than brightness, move into their crossing, and strike the exposed central bearing while both wing pairs pause; staying between matching glyphs triggers the lock.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Messenger lines and Guardian diameters can be assigned to one rotating axis, but entering the unlike-glyph quadrant interrupts those lower formations with the Warden's stalled rings.

monsters.name: Archon
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Compose line, diameter, and double-axis rules through three wing pairs and interlocking halo rings while a blank mask visibly turns toward the active command.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach ordered deconstruction: each wing pair owns one inherited geometry and one mask seam; breaking that seam permanently removes the corresponding ring from the composition.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Threefold Office: the upper wings and outer ring route Messenger decrees, the middle wings and shield-sized ring brace Guardian diameters, and the lower wings and inner crossed rings sustain a Warden injunction. The faceless mask rotates one third-turn toward the active office, exposing the opposite retaining seam while the sword of source-native pure light follows only that geometry.
monsters.telegraph: One pair among six wings opens to full symmetry, its halo ring advances, the blank mask turns exactly one third, and the pure-light sword flattens into the selected line or axis.
monsters.counterplay: Identify the moving wing pair and familiar geometry, take its learned safe space, then strike the opposite mask seam; each broken seam stops one ring and leaves that wing pair lowered.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Its three offices command Messenger ribbons, Guardian diameters, and Warden axes; breaking the corresponding mask seam ends that lower-form geometry and removes one ring from the Archon's pattern.

monsters.name: Seraph
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a four-orbit boss arena through layered wings and a working orrery halo, issuing and combining lower-form geometries until destroyed axles permanently reduce both orders and bodily abstraction.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of straight decrees, braced diameters, intersecting glyphs, and threefold offices while making every successful axle break remove an orbit, wing tier, and phase rule.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Living Orrery: four halo orbits turn around the Seraph's mostly luminous body. The Word orbit calls Messengers to draw radial ribbons; the Guard orbit places Guardians on a diameter; the Warden orbit counter-rotates paired script axes; and the Archon orbit combines two surviving orders under a six-wing marshal. Wings beyond counting are layered into four readable tiers, each bracing one orbit through a visible gold axle. The Seraph covers the active orbit with three wing tiers but must open the matching tier to issue its command. Striking that axle during the learned lower-form safe window destroys the orbit, dismisses its command, and causes one entire wing tier to fold into the body's clearer humanoid outline. After two breaks, the remaining orbits slow and run sequentially rather than together.
monsters.telegraph: One orrery orbit stops against a gold axle, its matching tier among the many wings opens like measured shutters, sacred script names the selected geometry, and the lower Celestials assume their familiar symmetric positions.
monsters.counterplay: Read the chosen orbit and lower-form formation, enter its learned safe line or quadrant, then strike the exposed gold axle before the wing tier closes; each destroyed orbit permanently removes a command and makes later phases slower, more sequential, and more humanoid.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Messengers, Guardians, Wardens, and an Archon each operate one orrery orbit; destroying its axle dismisses that formation, removes the linked wing tier, and prevents the Seraph from issuing the order again.

monsters.name: Screecher
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe attention from a low cliff perch, forcing a brief facing choice before a shallow talon pass.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the family announces its flight lane through crest, throat, and wing posture before leaving the perch.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Startle Cry: the Screecher inhales toward one target, shrieks, then makes a single low pass only if that target remains facing the perch.
monsters.telegraph: Its patchy crest flattens, bare throat expands, and half-molted wings point down the chosen lane.
monsters.counterplay: Turn or step behind cover during the inhale, then punish the thin talons when the aborted pass lands awkwardly.

monsters.name: Talon
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat reliable aerial pressure by hooking a target toward an exposed cliff lane and releasing before a second pass.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to watch planted talons and wing spread, then deny the straight carry rather than chase the flyer.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Cliff Hook: the Talon plants one hooked claw, spreads full brown wings, and rakes the other claw through a fixed carry line.
monsters.telegraph: Bone beads pull taut, one talon closes on stone, and the opposite leg extends beneath fully spread wings.
monsters.counterplay: Cross behind the planted leg or strike it before launch; a missed hook forces both wings low during recovery.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: A Screecher can mark the carry lane with its cry, but breaking the Talon's planted foot leaves both lower forms exposed on the same perch.

monsters.name: Skyrender
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the encounter by cutting one aerial lane into two crossing threat windows with independently banded wing tips.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read asymmetric wing bands and occupy the quiet wedge between two sequential passes.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Rend the Sky: the Skyrender paints one lane with the bright left wing band, climbs, then crosses it with the right wing and spear-length talons; only their intersection is trapped, while the wedge behind the dim wing remains safe.
monsters.telegraph: Its raised crest turns toward the crossing point while one iridescent wing-tip band flashes, followed by the opposite band at a different angle.
monsters.counterplay: Match the first band to its lane, move into the dim-wing wedge, and strike the overextended second wing root after the crossing pass.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Screechers hold attention on the first lane and Talons drag targets toward the crossing, but displacing either lower form leaves the safe wedge open.

monsters.name: Matriarch
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Marshal a rotating flock formation, protecting one lower flyer with ceremonial plumage while attacking from the opposite edge.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach formation rotation: read the gold ankle ring that owns the current guard and punish the uncovered trailing wing.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Ceremonial Mantle: the Matriarch wraps cloak-like plumage around one lower Harpy, then rotates the flock one quarter-turn and attacks from the open side with the opposite talon.
monsters.telegraph: Its elaborate crest leans toward the protected flyer, one gold ankle ring lifts, and braided trophy feathers sweep around that side.
monsters.counterplay: Move opposite the raised ring, separate the sheltered flyer, or strike the trailing wing before the rotation completes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: It shelters Screechers, Talons, or a Skyrender in turn; each uses its learned lane from the protected edge, so removing that lower form shortens the rotation.

monsters.name: Sky Queen
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a cliff-arena boss across four destructible perches, composing every lower-form lane before successive perch breaks force closer, simpler phases.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of cry facing, planted hooks, crossing bands, and flock rotation while turning the Queen's enormous wing span into a readable arena mechanism.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Court of Four Cliffs: the Sky Queen spans opposite perches with storm-colored wings and assigns a Screecher, Talon, Skyrender, or Matriarch to each gold-cuffed ledge. One crown feather names the active courtier, whose familiar mechanic establishes a lane; the Queen then closes one wing across it. Destroying the exposed cuff anchor drops that perch, dismisses its courtier, and tears one long primary from the Queen's span. At two remaining perches she must land between commands; at one she loses the loose-feather halo and fights with short committed talon sweeps.
monsters.telegraph: The full crest-crown raises one named feather, a matching gold cuff rings against its perch, ordinary loose feathers align around the selected lower form, and one enormous wing unfolds across the announced lane.
monsters.counterplay: Use the selected lower form's learned safe response, then strike the revealed cuff anchor while the spanning wing is committed; every broken perch permanently removes one command and narrows the Queen's reach.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Each of the four perches binds one Screecher, Talon, Skyrender, or Matriarch command to the Queen; destroying that perch removes the lower form and its associated boss lane for the remainder of the fight.

monsters.name: Bull-kin
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe commitment reading with one rangy overhead maul strike that cannot change direction after the hoof plants.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that horn and weapon size matter less than the visible loaded hoof and exposed recovery side.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Young Swing: the Bull-kin drags its wooden maul into a single overhead line after planting one hoof.
monsters.telegraph: The rope harness tightens, short stubby horns dip, and one unarmored hoof stamps behind the maul head.
monsters.counterplay: Cross the unloaded side and strike the bare back while the wooden maul rebounds from the floor.

monsters.name: Charger
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat front-line pressure through a fixed horn charge followed by a single-bladed axe sweep on the outside flank.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to cross behind the inside horn and punish the axe's opposite recovery rather than retreat in the lane.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Capped Run: iron horn caps define a straight charge; on impact or miss, the Charger pivots only toward its axe side.
monsters.telegraph: The brass nose ring stops swinging, the thick neck lowers, and both iron-capped horns align before the hooves accelerate.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the fixed lane toward the non-axe side, then attack the exposed neck before the one-way pivot finishes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Bull-kin maul lines can discourage the safe side, but interrupting the young carrier restores the Charger's learned crossing route.

monsters.name: Labyrinth Warrior
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the fight by dragging chained bronze plate into a temporary labyrinth wall, redirecting movement before striking around its corner.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the Specialist edits routes rather than merely hitting harder: follow chain slack to predict which corridor remains open.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Bronze Turn: the Warrior unhooks one chained plate, plants it as a wall, and pulls the chain around a horn wider than its shoulders to swing the wall ninety degrees; its one-handed greataxe covers only the closing side.
monsters.telegraph: Chained plate drops from the torso, the chain wraps one broad horn, and the greataxe moves to the side the wall will close.
monsters.counterplay: Move through the slack-chain corridor, sever the exposed hinge, or cross the non-axe corner while the wall rotates.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Chargers run the corridor the wall preserves and Bull-kin cover its hinge; breaking the chain collapses both routes into open ground.

monsters.name: Arena Champion
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control a circular arena lane by orbiting a chained stone block around a bronze-repaired horn and converting family walls into moving hazards.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach timing through chain tension: enter after the block passes, then break trophies that balance the next orbit.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Champion's Orbit: the re-forged horn serves as a chain guide while the stone block makes one accelerating circuit; each trophy on the harness acts as a counterweight and can be destroyed to shorten the arc.
monsters.telegraph: The bronze horn catches the chain, arena trophies lift from the harness, and the block grinds a bright circular line before leaving the floor.
monsters.counterplay: Step inside the circuit after the block passes, break a lifted trophy, and attack the repaired horn when the shortened chain snaps slack.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Labyrinth Warriors place walls that redirect the orbit while Chargers occupy exits; each destroyed counterweight makes those lower-form setups less effective.

monsters.name: Bull Emperor
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a five-gate boss arena, using gateway-wide horn arcs to rotate wall, charge, and orbit patterns until each broken horn band removes a gate and strips the imperial phase.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test mastery of loaded hooves, fixed charges, slack-chain corridors, and orbit timing while making arena destruction permanently simplify the fight.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Imperial Labyrinth: five bronze horn bands correspond to five shattered arena gates. The Emperor points its massive greataxe to assign Bull-kin to a hinge, Chargers to a lane, a Labyrinth Warrior to rotate a gate wall, or an Arena Champion to orbit a central block. The family-native brazier-like eye glow brightens only as a ceremonial command tell. After each formation resolves, the responsible band unlocks on the inside horn; breaking it drops one gate, removes that command, and cracks away one slab of bronze armor. At two gates the Emperor abandons command and makes slow, cape-dragging horn sweeps across the open floor.
monsters.telegraph: One horn band rings, the hide cape pulls toward its matching gate, the brazier-like eyes brighten without flame, and the chosen lower form takes its learned starting posture.
monsters.counterplay: Use the named lower-form response, cross behind the loaded horn, and break the unlocked inner band; every broken band permanently opens an arena route and removes one imperial command.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Bull-kin hold hinges, Chargers run gates, Labyrinth Warriors turn walls, and Arena Champions orbit blocks; the matching broken horn band dismisses that formation for all later phases.

monsters.name: Serpentling
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe spacing with a short coil recoil and one low blowgun or sling shot from a plainly two-armed, hoodless silhouette.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read the outer coil as both launch spring and recovery weak point.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Short Recoil: the Serpentling tightens its slim tail into one loop, fires, and snaps backward along that exact curve.
monsters.telegraph: Plain dull scales overlap at one outer seam while the bare torso leans inside the small coil.
monsters.counterplay: Step inside the recoil curve and strike the lifted outer seam before the hoodless Serpentling straightens.

monsters.name: Coilguard
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Hold a repeatable curved front line by bracing longer coils and threatening opposite arcs with two curved daggers.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the two armed arcs leave the coil interior safe during a committed crossed cut.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Crossed Crescent: the two-armed, hoodless Coilguard plants patterned coils and sweeps twin daggers from the outer curve toward one crossing point.
monsters.telegraph: Simple gold arm bands touch, both curved blades turn inward, and the patterned outer coil flattens against the floor.
monsters.counterplay: Enter the coil interior before the blades cross or strike the flattened outer scale row to break the brace.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: A Serpentling can fire across the guarded crescent, but entering the coil interior disrupts both its recoil curve and the Soldier's crossing point.

monsters.name: Hooded Adept
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the fight by using the first hood and second arm pair to reorder three marked coil segments into a temporary movement rule.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that added anatomy changes the mechanic: follow which of four hands owns each glyph, not merely the brighter scale pattern.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Three-Glyph Coil: the upper hands reveal the broad cobra hood and place Start and End glyphs while the lower hands rotate one jeweled spine segment between them; crossing the segments out of order tightens the surrounding coil, but striking the hand holding the middle glyph breaks the rule.
monsters.telegraph: The first broad hood fans open, four hands separate into upper and lower pairs, and three jeweled scale inlays brighten in a readable sequence.
monsters.counterplay: Read the hand-owned order, cross Start-middle-End, or interrupt the lower hand carrying the middle glyph before the coil closes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Serpentling shots travel from Start and Coilguards hold End; breaking the middle glyph also releases those lower forms from the scripted route.

monsters.name: Temple Guardian
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Guard a temple threshold through three paired weapon postures, changing which coil opening is safe without changing the authored doorway.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to pair hand posture with gold coil band and exploit the unarmed transition between three thresholds.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Sixfold Threshold: each pair among six arms holds one weapon posture, and gold banding along the full coil maps that posture to left, center, or right threshold; the ornate brow jewel turns before the active pair swaps.
monsters.telegraph: The brow ornament rotates, one of three gold coil bands lifts, and the corresponding arm pair crosses weapons over its threshold.
monsters.counterplay: Move through a band not matched to the raised pair and strike the brow jewel during the unarmed handoff.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Coilguards occupy the two inactive thresholds and a Hooded Adept may script one swap; disrupting the brow jewel opens every lower-form gap at once.

monsters.name: Serpent Empress
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a four-relic temple boss whose enormous coils redraw the arena around lower-form stations until broken gold bands ground each orbit and shorten the sovereign body.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test coil, blade, glyph, and threshold reading while every successful relic grounding permanently simplifies both arena and silhouette.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Crown of Four Relics: the gem-studded hood-crown aligns four floating relics on visible gold tracks around the torso. The Dart relic directs Serpentling fire, the Crescent relic arms Coilguard arcs, the Script relic sets an Adept sequence, and the Gate relic closes a Guardian threshold. The Empress's coils fill four concentric lanes, one per relic. When a known pattern resolves, its track hinge opens at the outer coil; breaking it grounds the relic, dismisses that lower form, and forces the corresponding coil ring to unwrap into a straight vulnerable length. At two relics the headdress drops and commands resolve one at a time.
monsters.telegraph: One hood gem aligns, its relic travels on a visible gold track, the corresponding coil band rises, and the named lower form assumes its familiar posture.
monsters.counterplay: Use the selected lower-form response, reach the exposed outer-track hinge, and break it; each grounded relic permanently removes one command and opens one concentric lane.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Serpentling, Coilguard, Hooded Adept, and Temple Guardian each operate one relic and lane; grounding that relic dismisses its lower form and removes its command for the rest of the boss.

monsters.name: Scout
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe lateral spacing with one bone-spear feint whose true thrust follows the counterbalancing tail.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the tail reveals attack direction before the spear and leaves the no-crest initiate exposed if displaced.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Countertail Jab: the Scout swings its long tail opposite the upcoming spear thrust, committing both body axes.
monsters.telegraph: Ordinary mud flakes from the lean body, the simple hide wrap twists, and the long tail sweeps away from the bone spear.
monsters.counterplay: Step toward the moving tail rather than the spear and strike the planted rear foot during the fixed jab.

monsters.name: Warrior
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Hold a repeatable close line with a woven shield while an obsidian-toothed club attacks around one side.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read shield weave tension and cross the unpainted side before the club follows.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Reed Lock: the Warrior bows its woven shield into an angled brace, then swings the toothed club only along the war-painted snout side.
monsters.telegraph: Reed fibers pull taut, the low forming crest rises, and snout paint aligns with the club shoulder.
monsters.counterplay: Cross the unpainted shield edge or cut its taut reed binding, exposing the torso before the club can reverse.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Scouts jab past the braced shield, but cutting its weave also exposes their predictable countertail lane.

monsters.name: Spineback
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the encounter by turning heavy dorsal spines into a one-way mobile gate that partitions the battlefield while twin blades threaten its open hinge.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that natural plating now edits space: follow which spine row lowers and attack through that temporary gate.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Spine Gate: the Spineback crouches and fans alternate dorsal spines into a barrier, leaving one visibly lowered segment as a passage; twin obsidian blades cover only the alligator-jaw side of that passage.
monsters.telegraph: Heavy dorsal spines rise in sequence, chest plate-scales lock, the alligator jaw opens toward one side, and one spine segment remains flat.
monsters.counterplay: Pass through the flat segment from the side opposite the jaw, strike its exposed root, or force the Specialist to turn and collapse the gate.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Warriors brace the closed spine segments and Scouts stab through gaps; breaking the lowered root folds the barrier and removes their protected lanes.

monsters.name: Swamp Chieftain
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a rotating hunting ring, using a tail-club and trophy skulls to assign lower forms to the open segment.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read headdress and tail commitment, then break the trophy tied to the active formation.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Four Hunts: four trophy skulls hang from crocodilian shoulder plating. The Chieftain strikes one with its tail-club to assign Scout jabs, Warrior shields, or Spineback gates to a quarter-ring, then sweeps only that marked quarter.
monsters.telegraph: The feather headdress tilts, one skull rattles, and the heavy tail-club draws a groove toward the selected quarter.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the marked quarter, cut its hanging skull during the tail recovery, and use the resulting gap in the lower-form ring.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Each trophy calls Scouts, Warriors, or a Spineback into a familiar duty; destroying it removes that quarter's formation until the encounter ends.

monsters.name: Saurian Tyrant
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Transform a five-mark hunting ground through a full back-sail crest, ordering lower forms until each cut mantle tie lowers one sail section and removes a phase rule.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test tail direction, shield weave, spine gates, and trophy quarters while permanent sail collapse turns a formation boss into a readable grounded duel.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Five Marks of the Sail: five painted panels on the full back-sail map to arena markings. Bone calls Scouts across one line, Reed braces Warriors, Obsidian raises a Spineback gate, Skull orders a Chieftain quarter, and Stone commits the Tyrant's own tail-club through the surviving marks. The ceremonial feather-and-hide mantle is tied once beneath each panel. After the selected learned pattern resolves, its tie stretches across the dorsal gap; cutting it folds that sail panel, erases the mark, and removes the command. With two panels left, the mantle falls and the Tyrant must plant before every tail sweep.
monsters.telegraph: One body-painted sail panel rises, the matching mantle tie pulls taut, its arena mark is exposed, and the chosen lower form assumes its known posture.
monsters.counterplay: Use the selected lower-form response, reach the exposed dorsal tie, and cut it; every collapsed panel permanently removes one command and opens that section of the arena.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Scout, Warrior, Spineback, and Swamp Chieftain each occupy a painted sail mark; cutting that panel's tie ends the linked lower-form pattern for all later phases.

monsters.name: Worker
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe route awareness by carrying one resin pellet between comb markers while avoiding direct confrontation.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that breaking the carried material changes later hive paths, and that the thin wingless form is weakest at its loaded middle limbs.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Work Trail: the Worker presses a resin pellet onto one floor node, creating a short visible route another Insectoid may follow faster.
monsters.telegraph: Its dull matte abdomen lowers, thin middle limbs cradle the pellet, and small mandibles point toward the chosen comb marker.
monsters.counterplay: Strike the exposed middle joint or destroy the pellet before placement; the wingless Worker hunches and retreats without a route.

monsters.name: Soldier
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Hold a repeatable hive lane by bracing natural forelimb blades along an existing resin route.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the darker wingless Soldier commits both blade limbs to a marked path and exposes its narrow waist from the side.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Route Shears: the Soldier follows one resin trail, plants behind its larger mandibles, and closes elongated forelimbs across the path like shears.
monsters.telegraph: Hardened carapace lowers, both natural blades open around the resin line, and the narrow waist twists square to it.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the marked route, attack the exposed waist from the side, or erase the resin node to end the guided close.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Workers extend routes for Soldiers; destroying the active pellet removes the Soldier's guided lane and forces ordinary movement.

monsters.name: Elite Drone
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the encounter by opening alternating spiracle circuits beneath closed wing cases, switching a resin route between pull and push behavior.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read side-specific vents and wing-case seams: the Specialist changes route function rather than simply strengthening it.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Hive Breath: the four-armed Drone keeps its wing cases closed while left spiracles pull units toward a marked resin node and right spiracles push them away; opening one vent bank seals the other and exposes the matching case seam.
monsters.telegraph: Glossy ridged plating lifts along one side, visible spiracles dilate, four arms brace the abdomen, and one closed wing-case seam separates.
monsters.counterplay: Move with the announced pull or push, then strike the open-side case seam before the vents switch; the opposite side remains inert.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Worker pellets become pull or push nodes and Soldiers brace on the selected side; breaking the case seam returns all routes to inert markings.

monsters.name: Royal Guard
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Patrol a three-dimensional lattice, using its first functional wings and ceremonial spear to defend one hive route from above.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to pair wing membrane tension with spear angle, then attack the exposed root after the committed descent.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Royal Lattice: the Guard connects three resin nodes by flying between them, then dives its spear along only the tautest edge; breaking any node slackens that edge and forces a landing.
monsters.telegraph: Crimson-and-gold shell ridges align, translucent functional wings pull one lattice edge taut, and the ceremonial spear turns along it.
monsters.counterplay: Destroy the announced node or leave the taut edge, then strike the wing root when the Guard lands to reset the lattice.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Workers maintain nodes, Soldiers hold ground edges, and Elite Drones reverse one lattice side; removing its node grounds all three duties locally.

monsters.name: Hive Queen
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Operate a stationary production boss whose immense wingless abdomen feeds four wax-comb chambers, each generating or modifying a lower-form duty until permanently disconnected.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test resin routes, blade lanes, vent switching, and aerial lattices while each destroyed abdomen valve removes one production branch and opens the throne.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Four Comb Broods: the wingless Queen's immense segmented abdomen connects through four visible resin valves to a wax-comb throne. The Work chamber produces a Worker and resin pellet, Blade hardens a surviving Worker into a Soldier, Breath molts a Soldier into an Elite Drone with closed cases, and Royal opens one Drone's cases into a Royal Guard. Tiny useless limbs cannot defend the valves, so attendants reposition the abdomen toward the selected chamber. Breaking the filled valve permanently collapses that comb and prevents its production. At two chambers the abdomen splits at exposed segment seams and every remaining cycle slows.
monsters.telegraph: Crown-like head plating turns toward one comb, attendants pull the wingless abdomen, translucent resin fills its valve, and the corresponding lower-form silhouette appears behind wax cells.
monsters.counterplay: Use the announced lower-form response to reach and rupture the filled valve; each collapsed chamber permanently ends that production path and exposes another abdomen seam.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Workers, Soldiers, Elite Drones, and Royal Guards are produced or promoted through four separate comb chambers; destroying a chamber ends that lower-form path for the rest of the boss.

monsters.name: Crawler
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe close-range attention with one dog-sized pounce from a pure spider silhouette.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the six eyes align before launch and the thin rear legs remain punishable after a missed pounce.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Cluster Pounce: the Crawler aligns six simple eyes, lowers its dull brown abdomen, and jumps along their shared gaze.
monsters.telegraph: All six eyes face one point, dripping fangs close, and the thin rear legs compress beneath the abdomen.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the eye line and strike the extended rear joints after landing; no humanoid torso or hand action is involved.

monsters.name: Stalker
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat ambush pressure by stretching one visible tripline between barbed legs and following with venomous fangs.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the first web decoration is a physical lane: cut the origin or cross behind the abdomen.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Barbed Line: the pure-spider Stalker hooks silk between two barbed forelegs, sweeps the tripline forward, and bites only targets it catches.
monsters.telegraph: Bright abdomen patterning flattens, venom-slick fangs lift, and ordinary silk tightens between two barbed legs.
monsters.counterplay: Cut the visible line at either leg or step behind the abdomen while both forelegs remain spread.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Crawlers pounce along the tripline gaze, but cutting either anchor exposes both spiders' thin loaded joints.

monsters.name: Weaver
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the encounter by using the first humanoid torso and hands to reweave two existing lines into a temporary safe-and-danger pattern.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the added torso changes thread authorship: follow hand crossings and eye pairs rather than treating the Weaver as a larger spider.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Handed Loom: the Weaver's humanoid hands cross two silk lines around silk-wrapped blades. Four pairs among eight bright eyes follow four resulting quadrants; the quadrant watched by mismatched eye colors remains safe while the other three tighten.
monsters.telegraph: The first humanoid torso rises, both wrapped blades cross, two spinneret lines enter the hands, and eight eyes separate into four readable pairs.
monsters.counterplay: Enter the mismatched-eye quadrant and cut the lower hand's thread or strike the exposed torso waist while the three other lines pull taut.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Crawler eye lines and Stalker triplines supply the two threads; removing either lower form leaves one entire side of the pattern slack.

monsters.name: Broodmother
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control successive web zones by carrying three visible egg sacs, releasing spiderlings to repair one damaged line while silk robes mark the next protected area.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach prioritization: identify the jeweled eye setting linked to the active sac, then prevent repair rather than clearing every spiderling.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Three Broods: each egg sac connects by woven-silk robe seam to one jeweled eye setting. The selected sac releases tiny spiderlings that rebuild a Crawler gaze, Stalker tripline, or Weaver quadrant; breaking its eye setting makes that brood scatter harmlessly.
monsters.telegraph: One jeweled eye setting turns, the matching robe seam pulls taut across the humanoid torso, and spiderlings gather on its egg sac.
monsters.counterplay: Break the linked eye setting or cut the taut robe seam before the spiderlings reach the damaged line; each spent sac stays collapsed.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Its three broods repair the learned mechanics of Crawlers, Stalkers, and Weavers; disabling the linked eye setting permanently removes that repair duty.

monsters.name: Weaver Queen
