monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a four-arch web cathedral whose silk drapery and lower-form knots reconfigure the arena until each severed throne anchor collapses an arch and simplifies the sovereign loom.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test eye lines, triplines, handed patterns, and brood repair while making every correct cut permanently reduce web topology, leg reach, and command options.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Cathedral Loom: four legs arch like columns around a layered-web throne, each tied to a silk drapery panel and lower-form knot. Gaze calls Crawlers down one aisle, Barb sets Stalkers across another, Hand lets a Weaver cross two aisles, and Brood lets a Broodmother repair a cut. The crown's clustered family-native eye glow identifies one knot, while humanoid hands pull only its drapery. After the learned lower-form pattern, that arch's throne anchor is exposed; severing it collapses the panel, dismisses the lower form, and forces the corresponding giant leg flat. With two arches left, the Queen descends from the throne and can weave only one aisle at a time.
monsters.telegraph: One crown-eye cluster aligns, its drapery panel tightens behind the humanoid torso, the linked arch rises, and the selected lower form assumes its familiar posture at the knot.
monsters.counterplay: Use the announced lower-form safe response, reach the exposed throne anchor, and sever it; each collapsed arch permanently removes one command and opens that cathedral aisle.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Crawler, Stalker, Weaver, and Broodmother each own one silk knot and arch; severing the matching throne anchor dismisses that form and prevents its web rule from returning.

monsters.name: Droplet
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe footwork with one tiny core-led hop and a short corrosive puddle.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the dark core chooses the landing point before the jelly follows.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Core Hop: the dark dot shifts to one side and the single pseudopod springs toward that line.
monsters.telegraph: The clear mass stretches behind the displaced dark core.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the core line and strike the overextended dot before the body recoils.

monsters.name: Blob
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat lane pressure by rolling swallowed debris toward its leading edge.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read internal contents as the next impact side.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Debris Roll: coins and bones gather ahead of the core before the knee-high mass surges.
monsters.telegraph: Cloudy jelly clears along one edge while coins and bones tumble toward it.
monsters.counterplay: Cross behind the debris line and hit the core through the newly clear rear wall.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Its wake gives Droplets a faster Core Hop, but crossing behind the Blob denies both lanes.

monsters.name: Ooze Knight
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a stance controller that moves its first humanoid crust between guard and thrust shapes.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that hardened shoulders protect only the side facing the crystalline chest core.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Crust Stance: shoulder crust flows into one arm-like brace, guarding a lane while leaving the opposite core edge clear.
monsters.telegraph: The glowing chest core slides under one shoulder and the crust audibly crystallizes there.
monsters.counterplay: Circle to the unarmored side and strike the exposed core edge before the brace liquefies and transfers.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Blob debris can reinforce the chosen brace; clearing the Blob keeps the exposed side soft.

monsters.name: Devourer
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control space by posing its suspended skeleton as a brace, cage, or striking frame.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that each armor plate follows a visible bone and collapses when that bone is displaced.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Borrowed Frame: the full skeleton locks into one of three poses and absorbed armor plates float onto its load-bearing bones.
monsters.telegraph: Bones rotate into alignment and matching armor plates click toward them through the jelly.
monsters.counterplay: Break the unplated pivot bone during commitment to collapse the pose and expose the core.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: It absorbs Blob debris to repair one plate; interrupting the debris roll prevents the repair.

monsters.name: Primordial Ooze
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Transform the arena into three moving tide basins while delegating distinct core patterns to lesser slimes.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test core reads, debris direction, crust stance, and skeletal pivots as the sovereign redistributes mass.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Transformation — Twelve-Core Tide: four cores enter each basin and command Droplet hops, Blob rolls, or Ooze Knight crust walls; clearing the announced pattern exposes that basin's lead core and permanently lowers its tide.
monsters.telegraph: Absorbed weapons form a face toward one basin while four of the dozen cores align beneath it and its tide rises.
monsters.counterplay: Answer the called lower-form pattern, then strike the aligned lead core; each broken lead core drains one basin and removes that command set.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Droplets, Blobs, and Ooze Knights carry one basin's learned rule; defeating them opens their aligned lead core instead of merely adding bodies.

monsters.name: Clay Figure
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe timing with one clumsy command-rune swing.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the scratched forehead rune fires before the uneven limb moves.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Wet Command: the single rune brightens and stiffens one fingerprinted arm for a delayed sweep.
monsters.telegraph: The forehead scratch lights while wet clay bunches at one shoulder.
monsters.counterplay: Step behind the stiffening arm and smear the exposed shoulder seam during recovery.

monsters.name: Stone Servant
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Hold a short front with fieldstone mass and alternating iron-bound joints.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the active iron band transfers load and leaves the opposite joint open.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Band Brace: one iron binding locks while the opposite stone arm repeats a reliable shove.
monsters.telegraph: One faint seam brightens and its iron band pulls tight.
monsters.counterplay: Strike the slack opposite band after the shove to separate two fieldstones.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Clay Figures attack from the braced side; breaking the band opens both lanes.

monsters.name: Rune Warrior
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a programmable combo whose torso runes visibly announce three ordered actions.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read engraved rune order and interrupt the unused final program.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Three-Line Program: torso runes illuminate from top to bottom for guard, anvil-fist, then ground pin; breaking the currently dark line deletes that future action.
monsters.telegraph: Three engraved torso rows light one at a time while the matching granite joint rotates.
monsters.counterplay: Attack the lowest still-dark rune between actions to shorten the sequence and expose both anvil fists.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Stone Servants brace the programmed lane; breaking their band removes the guard line.

monsters.name: Basalt Colossus
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control space by orbiting separated basalt plates between shield wall and crushing ring.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the native molten core is visible only when plate spacing changes.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Plate Orbit: floating basalt plates widen into a ring, exposing the molten chest core before converging on marked lanes.
monsters.telegraph: Joint gaps widen, plate edges align, and the molten core pulses through the chest cavity.
monsters.counterplay: Cross a widening gap and strike the core shutter before the plates converge.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Rune Warriors supply one program line to the orbit; deleting it leaves a permanent gap.

monsters.name: Master Golem
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a relief-carved arena that assembles and disassembles lower golem stations around a central monument.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test rune timing, band loads, program order, and plate gaps as permanent pieces of one authored boss arena.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Command — Master's Relief: the rune-halo selects a wall relief that produces a Clay Figure, Stone Servant, Rune Warrior, or plate pattern; solving that form's counterplay turns its relief inward and exposes one facet of the gemstone heart.
monsters.telegraph: One halo rune descends over a gold-inlaid relief while the matching heart facet refracts toward it.
monsters.counterplay: Answer the selected lower-form lesson and break the exposed heart facet; each broken facet permanently blanks its relief station.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Each lower form occupies one relief station; resolving its learned weak point converts that station into a permanent opening on the Master Golem.

monsters.name: Wisp
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe movement with one small airborne entity that commits to a visibly prepared destination.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the Wisp's tapered tail and a gathering eddy reveal its next drift before the core moves.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Trace Drift: the Wisp curls its lower tail toward a small gathering eddy, glides to that point as one continuous creature, and briefly dims on arrival.
monsters.telegraph: The asymmetric teardrop leans, its pointed crest bends, and its continuous lower tail curls toward the forming eddy.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the gathering eddy, follow behind the completed drift, and strike the dimmed binding seed before the body recovers.

monsters.name: Elemental Spirit
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Apply repeatable mid-range pressure with one committed arm channel.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the extended arm remains committed while the opposite side of the single core is exposed.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Tether Reach: one arm channel lengthens across a marked lane while the compact torso and opposite arm hold the binding core in place.
monsters.telegraph: The legless upper body narrows, one arm thins into a taut tether, and the core shifts visibly away from it.
monsters.counterplay: Cross behind the extending tether and strike the exposed side of the core before the arm retracts.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Wisps drift toward the tether endpoint; crossing behind the committed arm separates them from the Spirit.

monsters.name: Elemental Warden
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a lane controller whose two arm channels alternate between sweep and guard.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the attacking conduit fixes one lane while the opposite guard leaves one edge of the ring core exposed.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Twin Conduit: one arm becomes a sweeping affinity channel while the other compacts into a guard; the two roles reverse after every sweep.
monsters.telegraph: One conduit straightens toward the marked lane, the opposite arm folds inward, and one side of the ring core becomes visible.
monsters.counterplay: Enter behind the sweeping conduit and strike the exposed ring edge before the two arms reverse.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Elemental Spirits hold the guarded lane with Tether Reach; interrupting their tether opens the Warden's core flank.

monsters.name: Elemental Colossus
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control encounter space by shifting three articulated mantle sections between a barrier and converging marked lanes.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the core shutter is visible only while the three mantle sections widen and change formation.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Mantle Orbit: three affinity-built mantle sections widen into a barrier ring, expose the central shutter, and then converge through three marked lanes.
monsters.telegraph: The broad hovering body stills, three mantle sections separate along visible seams, and the central shutter turns toward the open gap.
monsters.counterplay: Cross a widening mantle gap and strike the exposed shutter before the three sections converge.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Elemental Wardens feed one conduit into each mantle lane; breaking the linked ring edge leaves that mantle gap open.

monsters.name: Elemental Sovereign
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Transform the arena through four binding patterns that recombine every lower-form lesson.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test drift destinations, committed tethers, alternating conduits, and mantle gaps as permanent stages of one authored boss encounter.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Transformation — Fourfold Lattice: four core facets successively invoke Trace Drift, Tether Reach, Twin Conduit, and Mantle Orbit; resolving a pattern permanently dims its facet and weakens the final lattice.
monsters.telegraph: One of four core facets turns outward, its matching orbital vane aligns with the arena, and the lower-form silhouette appears within the selected path.
monsters.counterplay: Resolve the announced lower-form lesson and strike the outward-facing facet; every dimmed facet removes one pattern from the final transformation.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Wisp, Elemental Spirit, Elemental Warden, and Elemental Colossus each govern one facet; solving that form's counterplay permanently disables its lattice pattern.

monsters.name: Sapling-walker
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe close footwork with one shallow-root lash.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the thin trunk must plant one shallow root before a branch can whip.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Shallow Plant: one root foot spreads and the opposite whip-like branch sweeps its narrow arc.
monsters.telegraph: Few leaves turn edge-on while one shallow root fans across the ground.
monsters.counterplay: Cross behind the planted root and strike the thin trunk before it pulls free.

monsters.name: Young Treant
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat frontal pressure with a mature canopy and alternating root-braced shoves.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that moss compression marks the loaded shoulder and opposite root opening.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Moss Brace: shoulder moss compresses as one branch arm and matching root perform a reliable shove.
monsters.telegraph: The proper leaf canopy tilts and moss darkens over the loaded shoulder.
monsters.counterplay: Move to the dry shoulder and punish the lifted opposite root after the shove.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Sapling-walkers lash from its shaded side; breaking the brace exposes both roots.

monsters.name: Oakheart
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a controller that braids hanging vines between heavy roots to define one moving safe lane.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to follow vine knots rather than canopy size and cut the single load-bearing braid.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Root Loom: two arm vines knot to one heavy root, drawing foliage walls together while the unknotted lane remains open.
monsters.telegraph: The clear bark face looks toward one root as two hanging vines twist around it.
monsters.counterplay: Take the unknotted lane and cut the visible braid at the selected root to drop both foliage walls.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Young Treants brace a wall; breaking their Moss Brace slackens one vine immediately.

monsters.name: Elder Warden
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control alternating habitats by opening an amber heartwood cavity that directs birds, mushrooms, and vine screens.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that resident life announces which ancient limb is active and leaves the cavity open after command.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Hollow Council: birds leave one branch, non-luminous mushrooms unfurl at one root and catch reflected amber heartwood light rather than emitting light, and a vine screen grows between them before the cavity releases amber sap.
monsters.telegraph: The hollow trunk opens, amber heartwood pulses, and mushrooms catch reflected amber heartwood light as residents move toward the selected branch-root pair; the mushrooms remain non-luminous.
monsters.counterplay: Cross outside the marked pair and strike the open heartwood cavity after the sap release.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Oakheart vine knots stabilize the screen; cutting their braid shortens the command.

monsters.name: World-Tree Warden
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Transform a four-grove arena by rerouting a back waterfall through boulder-bound roots and commanding learned lower-form habitats.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test root planting, canopy loads, vine lanes, and heartwood timing while every solved grove becomes permanently traversable.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Transformation — Four Seasonal Groves: the waterfall feeds one shoulder grove, boulders lock its root arch, and a lower form performs its learned rule there; resolving it exposes the supply root and drains that grove into a safe path.
monsters.telegraph: Waterfall flow bends toward one shoulder grove, its caught boulders grind, and the matching lower-form marker appears beneath the sky-filling canopy.
monsters.counterplay: Answer the called lower-form lesson, then sever the exposed supply root; each drained grove removes one command and opens the sovereign trunk.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Sapling-walker, Young Treant, Oakheart, and Elder Warden each govern one grove; solving that form's lesson permanently drains its route.

monsters.name: Sporeling
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe approach timing with one short dust puff after each planted step.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the plain cap tilts away from the safe side before dust releases.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Stub Step: a bulbous foot plants, the plain brown cap tips, and one faint nonpersistent dust puff marks the opposite side.
monsters.telegraph: The knee-high stalk compresses and its unlit cap edge lifts.
monsters.counterplay: Move under the lifted edge and strike the planted stalk after the puff.

monsters.name: Mycon
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat close pressure with a hardened stalk club and a readable gill-lit recovery.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the first faint gill light marks breathing cadence rather than an affinity attack.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Gill Beat: the spotted cap lifts, faint cyan gills inhale, and the hardened stalk club swings once before exhale.
monsters.telegraph: Faint gill light gathers while the human-sized stalk draws the club behind its body.
monsters.counterplay: Cross under the cap during inhale and punish the club-side stalk on exhale.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Sporelings puff on the exhale side; interrupting the Mycon leaves them uncoordinated.

monsters.name: Sporeguard
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a controller that writes inhaling and exhaling lanes through a constant thin spore cloud.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that visible mycelium veins and cloud density reveal when a lane draws inward or pushes outward.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Two-Breath Guard: shoulder spores alternately inhale along bright mycelium veins and exhale through the wide luminous cap, reversing safe movement.
monsters.telegraph: One side's veins brighten under translucent skin as its constant cloud narrows toward the gills.
monsters.counterplay: Move with the visible breath direction and cut the dim opposite vein during the reversal.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Mycons synchronize club swings to exhale; breaking their gill rhythm opens the reversing lane.

monsters.name: Fungal Shaman
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control three zones by writing temporary script in suspended spores and routing it through smaller arm mushrooms.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the lowest secondary cap authors the first stroke and remains vulnerable after writing.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Living Script: three smaller mushrooms pulse in sequence, drawing a visible spore glyph whose open stroke remains the safe route.
monsters.telegraph: One arm mushroom opens its gills and the parasol cap tilts toward the first suspended symbol.
monsters.counterplay: Follow the open glyph stroke and sever the first small mushroom stem before the script repeats.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Sporeguards supply the script cloud; thinning it makes every open stroke wider.

monsters.name: Mycelial Sovereign
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a throne-linked ground network that produces lower-form fruiting bodies at four readable nodes.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test cap tilt, gill cadence, cloud direction, and spore script while each solved node permanently severs arena control.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Production — Four Fruiting Nodes: the courtyard-wide cap lights one ground-mycelium route from the interlocked mushroom throne, producing the announced lower form; solving its lesson exposes that node beneath the drifting spore aurora.
monsters.telegraph: The aurora narrows over one network route, one throne mushroom opens, and the linked lower-form silhouette fruits at its endpoint.
monsters.counterplay: Resolve the announced lower-form rule, then sever the exposed mycelial node; every cut collapses one throne section and prevents that production pattern.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Sporeling, Mycon, Sporeguard, and Fungal Shaman each fruit from one node; its learned counterplay exposes the node for permanent removal.

monsters.name: Fishman
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe close spacing with a single hook rush followed by a visible gill recovery.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that gasping opens the dull-gray gill-neck after every committed cut.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Gasping Hook: the Fishman hunches behind a rusted hook or gutting knife, rushes once, then must flare its gills.
monsters.telegraph: Lidless eyes fix forward, webbed claws tighten, and neck gills pinch shut.
monsters.counterplay: Sidestep the weapon line and strike the flared gill-neck during the forced gasp.

monsters.name: Tidewarrior
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat spear pressure while coral chest armor protects one predictable approach.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the armor strap and fin flare reveal the spear's committed side.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Barbed Tide Line: the spear hooks a lane while the opposite finned forearm guards behind coral shards.
monsters.telegraph: Forearm and calf fins flare, one coral strap pulls tight, and the barbed spear lowers.
monsters.counterplay: Cross the unarmored side and cut the taut coral strap after the spear passes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Fishmen rush along the spear lane; cutting the strap exposes both their gill recoveries.

monsters.name: Abyssal Hunter
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a hunter that separates gaze from attack by casting its first small lure across the arena.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that lure direction and trident alignment are separate reads and the barnacled shoulder cannot turn quickly.
monsters.signatureMechanic: False Horizon: the brow lure illuminates one point while the broad eel-skinned Hunter sets a trident thrust toward the shadow opposite it.
monsters.telegraph: The small lure brightens, barnacles grind on one shoulder, and the trident rotates away from the light.
monsters.counterplay: Ignore the lure endpoint, cross outside the opposite trident line, and punish the rigid barnacled shoulder.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Tidewarriors hold the false-lit lane; breaking their coral strap reveals the Hunter's real thrust route.

monsters.name: Deep Priest
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control alternating zones by exposing source-supported translucent organs and routing pressure through jaw tentacles into a whale-bone staff.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that organ brightness announces which tentacle is load-bearing and which flank drains safely.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Organ Litany: one visible organ fills, the matching jaw tentacle grips a staff notch, and a pressure-scarred plate seals the selected zone.
monsters.telegraph: A translucent organ brightens while one beard tentacle coils around a whale-bone notch.
monsters.counterplay: Move to the dim-organ flank and sever the gripping tentacle after the zone releases.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Abyssal Hunters place lures on the selected zone; defeating one makes the corresponding organ drain early.

monsters.name: Leviathan Lord
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a four-quadrant court where kraken limbs and a crown of lures stage learned lower-form assaults.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test gill recovery, coral straps, false lures, and organ pressure while each solved court position removes one sovereign limb route.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Command — Fourfold Court: one crown lure names a quadrant, one kraken limb raises its net-and-kelp curtain, and a lower Deep One performs its learned rule; resolving it exposes that limb's sucker anchor.
monsters.telegraph: One crown lure brightens, the matching whale-scaled kraken limb lifts, and the lesser court assumes a familiar posture below.
monsters.counterplay: Answer the announced lower-form lesson and break the exposed sucker anchor; each broken anchor drops a curtain and permanently opens that quadrant.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Fishman, Tidewarrior, Abyssal Hunter, and Deep Priest each occupy one court quadrant; solving its lesson exposes and disables the linked kraken limb.

monsters.name: Afflicted
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe close spacing with one overlong grasp from a mostly human stance.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the patchy forearm tightens before the elongated fingers sweep and leaves the human wrist exposed.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Seam-Split Reach: one sleeve seam tears as the long fingers make a single hooking sweep.
monsters.telegraph: Wolfish yellow eyes fix on the target while patchy forearm fur rises beneath an intact but straining sleeve.
monsters.counterplay: Step inside the hooking fingertips and strike the exposed wrist before the sleeve settles.

monsters.name: Half-turned
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat a readable pounce from a crouched hybrid posture and reset through a vulnerable upright turn.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that muzzle direction names the pounce lane and the trailing cloth strip marks the recovery side.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Half-Turn Pounce: the hybrid drops its shoulders, lunges along the muzzle line, then must haul one not-yet-digitigrade leg underneath itself.
monsters.telegraph: The elongated snout lowers and fur across the back lifts as clothing strips trail straight behind.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the muzzle lane and punish the recovering rear leg before the crouch reforms.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Afflicted sweep at targets displaced by the pounce; breaking the Half-turned recovery opens both forms.

monsters.name: Werebeast
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a mobile hunter that crosses two claw lanes from different digitigrade footholds.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read hock compression, leave the second lane, and break the belt pivot rather than chase speed.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Hock Crosscut: one digitigrade leg plants for a low claw lane, then the opposite hock snaps the full beast through a crossing high lane.
monsters.telegraph: The thick pelt parts over one compressed hock while the ragged belt twists opposite the raised claws.
monsters.counterplay: Cross behind the first planted hock and sever or stagger the belt pivot before the second claw lane resolves.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Half-turned pounces herd targets into the first cut; interrupting their recovery leaves the crosscut without its setup.

monsters.name: Alpha
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control a rotating radius with the snapped chain while directing lower forms into exposed approaches.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the iron collar link bearing the chain load opens after every full rotation.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Broken-Moon Orbit: the Alpha whirls the snapped chain through one marked arc, then lunges through the opposite gap with oversized fangs.
monsters.telegraph: Moon-white eyes brighten, the scarred silver pelt flattens, and one iron collar link pulls visibly open.
monsters.counterplay: Follow the chain tail into the quiet gap and strike the loaded collar link before the lunge.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Werebeasts crosscut along the chain boundary; breaking the collar collapses their marked lanes.

monsters.name: Primal Beast-King
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Transform a four-quadrant hunting arena by shattering one binding rune and commanding a learned lower-form hunt in each phase.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test reach, pounce lanes, hock pivots, and collar openings while each solved hunt restores one restraint to the sovereign.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Transformation — Four Broken Bindings: the horn-and-antler crown points to one floating rune, the rune shatters, and an Afflicted, Half-turned, Werebeast, or Alpha performs its learned hunt before the King's matching limb fully transforms.
monsters.telegraph: One crown tine aligns with a binding rune, its fracture travels toward the matching limb, and the lower form assumes its familiar starting posture.
monsters.counterplay: Solve the announced lower-form lesson, then strike the exposed crown root before the limb locks; each restored binding removes one hunt and reduces the final transformation.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Afflicted, Half-turned, Werebeast, and Alpha each author one transformation phase; defeating or disrupting that form exposes the linked crown root.

monsters.name: Grotesque
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe approach timing with one short drop from a low architectural perch.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that chipped sandstone feet must release together and leave the crude wing roots immobile.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Chipped Drop: the perched Grotesque releases both claws for a low body slam, then scrapes back to its pedestal fragment.
monsters.telegraph: Crude features tilt down and dust falls from the chipped toe that bears the perch load.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the short drop lane and strike the loaded toe or tiny wing root during the scrape back.

monsters.name: Sentinel
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat short wall-to-floor hops that anchor a predictable claw line.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that moss compression and the small wing fold announce the landing claw.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Mossed Hop: granite legs push from a wall while small bat wings stabilize, never sustain, one blunt-claw landing.
monsters.telegraph: Weathered moss squeezes from one shoulder and the matching small wing unfolds halfway.
monsters.counterplay: Cross under the unwinged side and punish the mortar gap at the landing shoulder.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Grotesques drop into the Sentinel's landing lane; breaking its shoulder gap makes both land short.

monsters.name: Guardian
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a true aerial threat that traces one carved relief route before a broad-wing dive.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read amber joint order and step through the final unlit relief segment.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Cornice Route: amber seams illuminate shoulder, elbow, and ankle reliefs in order while broad functional wings bank toward the matching dive lane.
monsters.telegraph: The upright body turns, broad wings lock, and three amber seams light along one carved relief path.
monsters.counterplay: Track the seam order, cross through the unlit segment, and strike the wing hinge after the dive commits.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Sentinels occupy the first lit landing; breaking their wall-hop anchor erases that segment.

monsters.name: Cathedral Warden
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control alternating aisles by opening marble-and-bronze wing tracery as a load-bearing screen.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that bronze braces darken before each tracery aisle closes and can be broken from the open side.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Rose-Window Guard: one ornate wing frames a closing aisle while the opposite tracery panel vents through a water-spout mouth.
monsters.telegraph: Spired horns align with an aisle and verdigris bronze drains from the brace about to carry the marble wing.
monsters.counterplay: Take the open aisle and break the darkening bronze brace before the framed wing closes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Guardians dive along the framed aisle; breaking its brace forces them to land and exposes their hinges.

monsters.name: Stone Sovereign
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command an architectural boss arena where buttress wings, throne quadrants, and statuary attendants restage every learned load path.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test perch chips, hop hinges, relief routes, and tracery braces while each disabled attendant removes one throne support.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Command — Living Elevation: the throne rotates toward one of four statuary attendants, buttress wings frame that quadrant, and the attendant performs a lower-form rule before its pedestal becomes the sovereign's exposed support.
monsters.telegraph: One buttress wing settles onto the throne, the matching attendant lifts from the base, and familiar amber joints illuminate its source-form posture.
monsters.counterplay: Answer the attendant's learned tell and break its pedestal bond; each lost support opens a throne quadrant and limits the sovereign's wing span.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Grotesque, Sentinel, Guardian, and Cathedral Warden attendants each govern one elevation; solving their mechanic exposes the linked throne support.

monsters.name: Wisp-spirit
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe target reading with one vapor feint that resolves only when the half-face turns complete.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the faint inner glow condenses at a single vapor knot before the small rush.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Unfinished Glance: the half-face forms on one side of the vapor and darts along that gaze before dissolving.
monsters.telegraph: A faint warm point gathers beneath one unfinished eye while the opposite face remains smoke.
monsters.counterplay: Cross behind the forming eye and strike the dense vapor knot after the dart.

monsters.name: Lesser Djinn
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat a bounded two-arm pull from a defined torso and visible cuff anchors.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the plain cuff facing inward carries the binding load and opens after the pull.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Bound Draw: both solid arms pull a smoke line toward the bare torso while one plain gold wrist cuff tightens.
monsters.telegraph: The sash points forward, the torso sharpens, and one unadorned cuff rotates inward.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the draw line and strike the inward cuff before the torso softens back into smoke.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Wisp-spirits dart along the draw line; breaking the cuff disperses their vapor knots.

monsters.name: Djinn
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a directional controller that separates visible wind-arm direction from orbiting-ring release order.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read ring alignment, use the quiet vector, and interrupt the wrist gap rather than chase smoke.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Three-Wish Vector: three gold rings align around one visible wind forearm, then release pressure lanes in outer-to-inner order while the other arm stays still.
monsters.telegraph: Ornate sash tails stream in one direction and the three forearm rings click into visibly unequal spacing.
monsters.counterplay: Move through the still arm's lane and strike the widest ring gap before the inner release.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Lesser Djinn pull targets across the first vector; breaking their cuff interrupts the outer ring.

monsters.name: Great Djinn
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control alternating script zones through a giant storm-colored body without obscuring the readable binding glyph.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that crown direction selects a script and the final open glyph is the interrupt point.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Crowned Clause: the jeweled crown points to one sacred line written in vapor, and the giant body curls around that line until its final glyph closes.
monsters.telegraph: One crown jewel aligns with the floor while sacred script writes outward from the matching smoke shoulder.
monsters.counterplay: Cross outside the writing direction and break the final open glyph before the storm body closes around it.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Djinn ring vectors trace the selected clause; breaking a ring gap leaves its glyph permanently open.

monsters.name: Wish-Sultan
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Command a palace-scale vortex arena where four bound lamps stage learned lower-form clauses around a floating throne.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test vapor knots, cuff loads, ring vectors, and script gaps while each severed lamp tether simplifies the sovereign vortex.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Command — Four Bound Lamps: one lamp orbits to the throne front, its smoke robe forms a lower Djinn posture, and the vortex closes a corresponding court lane until that form's learned anchor is solved.
monsters.telegraph: The floating throne turns, one lamp descends on a visible gold tether, and the smoke robes adopt a familiar half-face, cuff, ring, or script silhouette.
monsters.counterplay: Answer the announced lower-form lesson and sever the exposed lamp tether; each freed lamp opens a court lane and removes one vortex command.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Wisp-spirit, Lesser Djinn, Djinn, and Great Djinn rules each bind one lamp phase; resolving the rule exposes that lamp's tether.

monsters.name: Pixie
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe attention with one palm-sized thorn thrust hidden behind a short dust trail.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the simple insect wings pause before the thorn commits and expose their shared root.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Dust Feint: a brief trail of glowing dust continues forward while the Pixie stops and thrusts its thorn across the trail.
monsters.telegraph: The simple insect wings close together and the gold dust stream continues one body length without the Pixie.
monsters.counterplay: Ignore the continuing dust and strike the shared wing root during the stopped thrust.

monsters.name: Sprite
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat fan-shaped pressure by folding layered petal wings around a knee-high thorn advance.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the outer petal closes first and leaves the inner seam exposed after the fan.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Garland Fan: layered petals close outer-to-inner while the thorn blade traces the same narrowing lane.
monsters.telegraph: Garland clothing draws tight and the outer petal layer tilts toward the selected side.
monsters.counterplay: Cross behind the outer petal and strike the inner wing seam after the blade passes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Pixies leave dust on the fan edge; breaking the petal seam disperses the feint.

monsters.name: Fae Knight
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a refractive lane controller whose stained-glass wings and branch antlers cast conflicting route signs.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to compare antler shadow with glass color and take the unreflected lane.
monsters.signatureMechanic: False Rose Path: one antler frames a colored wing pane, projecting three apparent thrust lanes while only the pane without an antler reflection carries the leaf-armored charge.
monsters.telegraph: The unnervingly still face turns last, one woven antler crosses a stained-glass pane, and two reflected lanes brighten.
monsters.counterplay: Take the pane with no antler reflection and strike the rigid wing rib after the charge passes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Sprites fan petals across reflected lanes; cutting their inner seam reveals the true pane early.

monsters.name: Fae Noble
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control alternating court sectors by turning a mask-like face while a mote court lifts one living-gown hem.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the crown and mask point in different directions and only the lifted gown seam carries the command.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Still Court: the thorn-and-blossom crown names one sector, the no-white eyes fix another, and motes lift the living leaf gown over the actual command lane.
monsters.telegraph: The mask face stays still as one gown hem rises and the hovering court condenses beneath it.
monsters.counterplay: Follow the lifted hem rather than the gaze and cut the exposed living seam after the court passes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Fae Knights project false lanes across the court; breaking their glass rib clears the commanded sector.

monsters.name: Fae Monarch
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Transform a four-season arena with impossible geometry while each crown quarter restages a learned lower-form deception.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test dust feints, petal seams, reflected paths, and court tells while each solved season restores one stable route through bent reality.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Transformation — Simultaneous Seasons: one quarter of the season crown turns toward the viewer, impossible wing geometry folds that quadrant, and a lower Fae performs its learned rule inside the faint reality bend.
monsters.telegraph: One seasonal crown quarter advances, a shattered-rainbow wing folds through an impossible angle, and the called lower form appears on the last stable line.
monsters.counterplay: Answer the lower-form tell and break the exposed crown quarter; each broken season straightens one arena route and removes that transformation.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Pixie, Sprite, Fae Knight, and Fae Noble each author one seasonal deception; resolving it exposes the linked crown quarter.

monsters.name: Crawler
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe timing with one scuttling route whose final thin limb appears to skip a contact point.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the last matte limb pauses at an open edge even though no reflection confirms its position.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Unfinished Step: too many thin limbs scuttle in sequence, but one missing contact makes the body hesitate before the low rake.
monsters.telegraph: Three limb tips align while a fourth open edge stops moving against the floor without reflection.
monsters.counterplay: Cross the missing-contact side and strike the paused thin-limb edge before the rake resumes.

monsters.name: Hollow
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat a humanoid advance that draws attacks toward a smooth face-hole before folding at one blurred edge.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the hole is a false center and the sharpest outer edge carries the committed strike.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Empty Regard: the face-hole fixes forward while one blurred shoulder edge becomes sharp enough to cut across its approach.
monsters.telegraph: The smooth face-hole narrows while every edge blurs except one shoulder line.
monsters.counterplay: Ignore the face-hole, cross the blurred side, and punish the sharp shoulder after it passes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Crawlers follow the sharp edge; interrupting their missing step reveals the Hollow's real shoulder early.

monsters.name: Fracture
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a geometry controller that folds the arena route differently from its orbiting eye cluster.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read the star-interior gap rather than eye direction and cross before the wrong fold closes.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Contradictory Fold: orbiting eyes mark two apparent hinges while the star-flecked interior opens at a third gap and folds the body through that route.
monsters.telegraph: The body bends the wrong way, the eye cluster pauses, and one star-field gap widens without an eye above it.
monsters.counterplay: Take the eye-less star gap and strike the exposed geometric hinge after the fold.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Hollows sharpen an apparent hinge; breaking that shoulder exposes the true star gap.

monsters.name: Encroacher
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control alternating arena margins with a vast form only partly present and negative limbs that stop before their endpoints.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the dissolving edge nearest the sharpest star gap is the only committed margin.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Before-It-Ends: one negative limb begins beyond the frame, stops before it ends, and subtracts a lane until the adjacent partial edge returns.
monsters.telegraph: A vast contour enters only part of the scene while one cold accent marks the partial edge that will return last.
monsters.counterplay: Move through the unmarked negative limb and strike the returning partial edge at its cold accent.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Fractures fold apparent exits toward the selected margin; breaking their hinge restores one lane.

monsters.name: Outer Sovereign
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Phase an arena around an unresolved sovereign absence whose eye ring restages each learned subtraction rule.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test missing contacts, false centers, wrong folds, and partial edges while every closed eye group restores one resolvable arena boundary.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Phase — Unfinishable Witness: one eye-ring interval opens, the world-shaped absence subtracts a quadrant, and a lower Void Horror performs its learned rule along the last resolvable boundary.
monsters.telegraph: A group of unblinking eyes closes in sequence while geometry refuses to resolve around the remaining open interval.
monsters.counterplay: Answer the called lower-form subtraction and strike the open eye-ring interval; each closed group restores a boundary and removes one phase route.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Crawler, Hollow, Fracture, and Encroacher each define one eye-ring phase; resolving that form's lesson exposes the associated interval.

monsters.name: Blank
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Probe close timing with one smooth unfinished reach from a deliberately generic stance.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the blank wrist briefly creases before featureless fingers extend.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Unpainted Reach: one clay-gray arm lengthens without a shoulder turn, then returns through a visible wrist crease.
monsters.telegraph: The smooth wrist dimples while the blank head with no face, hair, or clothing remains perfectly still.
monsters.counterplay: Step across the extending arm and strike the temporary wrist crease before it smooths.

monsters.name: Halfling Copy
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Repeat copied weapon pressure from a partial disguise whose one gray arm cannot complete the same motion.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the blurred mouth announces the copied strike while the unfinished arm remains the safe side.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Half-Learned Cut: the finished side copies a simple cut as the unformed gray arm attempts and fails to mirror it.
monsters.telegraph: The nearly right face blurs at the mouth and borrowed color drains toward the finished shoulder.
monsters.counterplay: Cross the unfinished-arm side and punish its smooth shoulder after the copied cut.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Blanks reach from the copied side; striking the unfinished shoulder exposes both wrist creases.

monsters.name: Mimic
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a reactive copy specialist that perfectly mirrors one action except for a wrong hand joint and jaw seam.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to offer a harmless motion, identify the anatomically impossible mirror, and attack the jaw seam during correction.
monsters.signatureMechanic: One Error Copy: the near-perfect human copy mirrors the target's last committed posture, but one hand bends the wrong way and pulls a faint jaw seam open.
monsters.telegraph: Borrowed clothing settles into exact symmetry while the wrong hand rotates one joint too far and the jaw seam pales.
monsters.counterplay: Feed a short recoverable motion, move opposite the wrong hand, and strike the open jaw seam before the copy corrects.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Halfling Copies repeat the offered motion imperfectly; interrupting their finished side delays the Mimic's correction.

monsters.name: Facewearer
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Control three alternating attack rules by rotating layered faces to the front of an otherwise flawless copy.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach that the rear mask edge moves before the next face and remains vulnerable after the transition.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Front in Turn: three layered faces rotate through the front position, each calling a learned reach, cut, or mirrored response while the vacated edge stays open.
monsters.telegraph: Two mask profiles slide backward and the third face becomes unnaturally still before its rule begins.
monsters.counterplay: Read the incoming profile, answer its familiar rule, and strike the trailing mask edge after it rotates away.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Blank, Halfling Copy, and Mimic each supply one face rule; disabling that lower form leaves its layer unable to close.

monsters.name: Faceless Sovereign
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Transform a copy arena through body-wide face processions while the mask crown commands learned lower-form defects.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test blank wrists, unfinished sides, wrong joints, and rotating mask edges while each removed crown mask strips one copied phase from the body.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Arena Transformation — Parade of Faces: one mask-crown segment lowers, body-wide faces stream from chest to arms and back, and the sovereign copies a lower Doppelganger rule until its source defect reaches the crown latch.
monsters.telegraph: Borrowed colors move across the smooth flesh, one crown mask tips forward, and the called lower-form defect appears on the last face in the procession.
monsters.counterplay: Answer the announced copied rule and strike the crown latch when its source defect arrives; each removed mask erases one procession and reveals more blank native flesh.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Blank, Halfling Copy, Mimic, and Facewearer each define one mask-crown phase; solving its defect exposes the linked latch.

monsters.name: Gray Wolf
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Circle toward an exposed side and commit to one tripping bite when the target turns away.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to track facing and deny a simple flank before learning full pack coordination.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Cross-Step Trip: the Gray Wolf crosses its outside forepaw inward before lunging at the target's rear leg.
monsters.telegraph: Its shoulders drop and the outside forepaw crosses inward while its gaze fixes on the exposed leg.
monsters.counterplay: Face the Wolf or step across its approach, then punish the missed bite during the low recovery.

monsters.name: Dire Wolf
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Alternate pursuit with a packmate and slow isolated prey with a committed rear-leg bite.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to break two-sided pursuit geometry instead of retreating in a straight line.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Alternating Hamstring: only the Wolf on the prey's rear quarter attacks while its partner widens for the next exchange.
monsters.telegraph: Its head flattens beside the shoulder as the partner visibly widens formation.
monsters.counterplay: Break their angle with terrain or stagger the committed biter before the partner completes the swap.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Gray Wolves probe the opposite flank and create the turn that lets the Dire Wolf claim the rear quarter.

monsters.name: Howler
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Change the pack's attack rhythm by advancing allies on one side while the opposite wing holds position.
monsters.teachingGoal: Introduce a qualitative pack-command pivot in which throat direction, not proximity alone, determines the next attack wing.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Directed Howl: one directional howl releases the indicated wing while every Wolf on the opposite side pauses and braces.
monsters.telegraph: Its pale throat ruff expands and its muzzle points directly toward the wing that will advance.
monsters.counterplay: Interrupt the inhale or cross through the temporarily stationary wing before the advancing side closes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Gray Wolves gain longer flank probes and Dire Wolves immediately swap pursuit sides when their wing is called.

monsters.name: Pack Alpha
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Mark one target, intercept attacks aimed at lesser Wolves, and swap the active pursuit wing after every lunge.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to separate a protective commander from the pack rather than tunneling into its guarded target.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Marked Quarry: a visible scent trail binds the Alpha's intercept to one target until terrain or distance breaks the line.
monsters.telegraph: Its tail locks level, nose paints a visible scent line, and one foreleg braces toward the marked target.
monsters.counterplay: Cross strong terrain to break the scent line or bait the intercept away before attacking the lesser Wolves.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: It intercepts for Gray Wolves, completes Dire Wolf pursuit swaps, and changes wings on the Howler's cue.

monsters.name: Greatwolf
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Tighten an arena-scale hunt circle and assign every lower Wolf form to a readable breach point.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test facing, pursuit swaps, howl direction, and commander separation as one coordinated pack encounter.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Closing Hunt: four breach points contract in sequence while the Greatwolf assigns Gray Wolves to probe, Dire Wolves to pin, the Howler to change tempo, and the Alpha to close the weakest exit.
monsters.telegraph: Hackles rise in sequence around the circle and the Greatwolf's broken upper canine points toward the next closing breach.
monsters.counterplay: Defeat or displace the assigned lower form and escape through its opening before the Greatwolf commits to that breach.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Each lower form owns one hunt-circle function; removing it keeps that breach open and permanently weakens the corresponding boss phase.

monsters.name: Scrub Bear
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Deliver one broad forepaw swipe after standing, then drop heavily onto all fours.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the family's basic promise that enormous commitment produces a generous recovery window.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Standing Swipe: the Bear rises, loads one shoulder, and sweeps once before an unavoidable heavy landing.
monsters.telegraph: Its hips settle and the striking shoulder rises above the other forepaw.
monsters.counterplay: Move under the raised side and punish the landing recovery from the rear quarter.

monsters.name: Cave Bear
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Advance behind crossed forelegs, absorb frontal pressure, then open into a two-paw maul.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to disengage from guarded frontal mass and seek a rear-quarter angle.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Crossed Maul: protected advance ends when both forearms open into a fixed two-swipe sequence.
monsters.telegraph: The forearms cross, claws scrape, and its chest expands before opening.
monsters.counterplay: Attack from the rear quarter or disengage until the second swipe exhausts and exposes the chest.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Scrub Bears pressure the exposed side while the Cave Bear's crossed advance fixes attention.

monsters.name: Hookclaw
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Hook a limb, shield, or obstacle and drag it sideways to break defensive formations.
monsters.teachingGoal: Introduce an asymmetric specialist whose dangerous side and planted recovery side must be read separately.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Hook and Haul: one enlarged curved claw catches the target while the opposite hind foot becomes a visible towing anchor.
monsters.telegraph: The hooked forepaw turns palm-up and the opposite hind foot digs deeply into the ground.
monsters.counterplay: Dodge toward the planted foot or strike the exposed inner wrist before the sideways drag begins.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Cave Bears block the obvious retreat while Scrub Bears harry targets displaced by the drag.

monsters.name: Scarback
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Bring down a tree, pillar, or boulder as moving cover before charging through the debris.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read the environment as part of the Bear's commitment and escape before the route closes.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Falling Territory: Scarback tests one structure, topples it into a fixed lane, then follows through the debris.
monsters.telegraph: Its broad back scars stretch while both forepaws test the chosen structure.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the fall lane or attack the planted hind legs before the structure gives way.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Lower Bears use the fallen structure as flank cover, but lose that advantage if the collapse is interrupted.

monsters.name: Ancient Ursine
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Claim three den landmarks and alternate roar, upheaval, and maul phases while commanding lesser Bears around the active landmark.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test committed-swipe windows, guarded fronts, grapple anchors, and terrain collapse as one territorial encounter.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Three Den Marks: the Ancient rubs one shoulder against a landmark to empower the matching lower-form behavior until that mark is broken.
monsters.telegraph: The marked shoulder sheds fur and pigment onto one landmark before the corresponding phase begins.
monsters.counterplay: Break the active mark or draw the pack to an unclaimed zone, then punish the Ancient's exposed rubbed shoulder.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Scrub Bears guard the roar landmark, Cave Bears hold the maul landmark, Hookclaw displaces intruders, and Scarback reshapes the route to the active mark.

monsters.name: Bristle Hog
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Make one short straight charge that cannot turn after a single scrape.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach the simplest charge tell and reward a lateral sidestep rather than backward retreat.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Two-Scrape Charge: one forehoof paws twice before the Hog launches along its fixed head line.
monsters.telegraph: The forehoof scrapes twice and the head lowers between the shoulders.
monsters.counterplay: Sidestep the fixed lane and punish the exposed flank during its stop.

monsters.name: Tunnel Boar
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Brace inside narrow ground and drive targets out of cover with a long committed charge.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to turn a dangerous lane into a collision by reading the full brace.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Tunnel Brace: both hind legs lock before a long charge that gains power in narrow terrain but cannot evade obstacles.
monsters.telegraph: Both hind hooves settle and dust funnels backward along the future lane.
monsters.counterplay: Leave the lane or make the Boar collide with solid terrain, exposing its stunned forehead and flank.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Bristle Hogs make short probes that encourage the target to enter the Tunnel Boar's longer lane.

monsters.name: Razorback
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Cut a curved furrow whose route controls the next charge and throws debris outward.
monsters.teachingGoal: Introduce a specialist whose charge can curve but must first draw its complete route into the ground.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Plow Curve: the inside tusk remains buried while the Razorback scores a visible curved path for its next charge.
monsters.telegraph: The inside tusk stays in the soil and back bristles ripple along the future curve.
monsters.counterplay: Cross the furrow before launch or strike the rooted outside leg while the curve is being cut.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Bristle Hogs rush across the outside edge while Tunnel Boars threaten the straight escape from the curve.

monsters.name: War Tusker
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Hook barriers, rotate them into new lanes, and signal lesser Boars to charge through the opening.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to protect or release movable cover before the Boar family weaponizes it.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Tusker's Gate: one tusk hooks a barrier while the neck rotates it, creating a new family charge route.
monsters.telegraph: The neck twists beneath the hooked object and the free tusk points down the intended lane.
monsters.counterplay: Release or destroy the object, or stagger the planted rear leg before the rotation locks.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Lower Boars immediately use the opened route, but collide or scatter if the gate is released before their charge.

monsters.name: Old Tusk
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Create three successive stampede lanes before personally collapsing the remaining safe route.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test straight lanes, collision terrain, curved furrows, and rotated barriers in one readable stampede puzzle.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Three-Lane Stampede: each tusk scores a lane and assigns Bristle Hogs, Tunnel Boars, or Razorbacks to lead it before Old Tusk takes the final gap.
monsters.telegraph: The mane rises from tail to skull and the assigned lane leader stamps once inside its scored route.
monsters.counterplay: Interrupt a lane leader to preserve its gap, then redirect Old Tusk into the disabled route's obstacle.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Each lower form leads one route type while the War Tusker reshapes cover; removing a leader permanently preserves that lane during the boss phase.

monsters.name: Soil Grub
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Travel just below the surface as a short moving ridge and emerge for one bite.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read subsurface travel from a simple fixed sequence of ground pulses.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Three-Pulse Bite: three evenly spaced soil pulses lead to one small emergence at the endpoint.
monsters.telegraph: Three compact soil humps travel in a straight line while the third widens around the head.
monsters.counterplay: Step perpendicular to the pulses and strike the soft body while it turns to re-enter the ground.

monsters.name: Burrowing Worm
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Cross a long underground lane, erupt beneath a target, and leave rear segments exposed while turning.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to avoid the forecast endpoint and punish the rear instead of attacking the armored head.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Moving-Ridge Eruption: an accelerating ridge ends in a vertical bite while the long rear body remains stranded above ground.
monsters.telegraph: A widening ridge accelerates and embedded pebbles jump at the eruption endpoint.
monsters.counterplay: Avoid the endpoint and attack the exposed soft rear segments during the slow turn underground.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Soil Grubs create short harmless-looking ridges that complicate attention without hiding the Worm's larger stone-displacing route.

monsters.name: Hookjaw Burrower
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Catch a target or terrain anchor between split jaws and tow it sideways toward a tunnel.
monsters.teachingGoal: Introduce a rescue and formation-displacement specialist with two separately breakable approach lines.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Converging Hooks: two jaw tips travel under separate cracks, surface around the target, and retract toward the same tunnel mouth.
monsters.telegraph: Paired ground cracks converge while both hooked jaw tips briefly break the surface.
monsters.counterplay: Break either convergence line or strike the exposed jaw hinge before the hooks close.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Soil Grubs crowd the open rescue line while Burrowing Worms threaten the predictable escape endpoint.

monsters.name: Tremor Worm
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Produce several decoy ridges while its heavy body travels beneath one real route, then erupt into a sweeping roll.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to distinguish cosmetic surface disturbance from the physical displacement caused by the true body.
monsters.signatureMechanic: False Tremors: three dust ridges advance, but only the true route moves embedded stones and ends in a body roll.
monsters.telegraph: False ridges shed loose dust while the real ridge displaces stones from below.
monsters.counterplay: Track the embedded stones, evade that eruption, and punish the hammer tail left above ground after the roll.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Lower Burrowers can occupy decoy routes, but their smaller ridge signatures remain distinct from the Tremor Worm's stone displacement.

monsters.name: Deep Maw
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Open persistent tunnel mouths, route lower Burrowers through them, and collapse one arena sector each phase.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test ridge reading, eruption endpoints, hook convergence, and true-route identification inside a controllable tunnel network.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Feeding Network: tunnel lips contract in sequence toward a selected collapse while Deep Maw exposes its feeding collar to command traffic.
monsters.telegraph: Tunnel mouths contract in an ordered wave and the pale collar plates flare behind the petaled maw.
monsters.counterplay: Block a feeder tunnel, evacuate the contracting sector, then strike the exposed collar before the network reroutes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Soil Grubs scout open mouths, Burrowing Worms erupt at endpoints, Hookjaws drag prey toward active routes, and Tremor Worms conceal the real collapse lane.

monsters.name: Wildcat
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Break line of sight once and pounce from the nearest low cover.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to watch cover disturbance and challenge a predictable first ambush.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Nearest-Cover Pounce: the Wildcat always uses the closest valid low cover after breaking sight.
monsters.telegraph: Its tail tip stops and the chosen cover edge parts immediately before launch.
monsters.counterplay: Face the opening or step toward it to force an early short pounce, then punish the landing.

monsters.name: Lynx
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Bound between raised perches and attack whichever target presents the longest exposed back.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to rotate facing vertically and contest predictable landing cones.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Perch Exchange: the Lynx uses two visible perches and must complete one grounded pause after each attack.
monsters.telegraph: Ear tufts flatten and the selected perch sheds dust toward its landing cone.
monsters.counterplay: Rotate toward the perch or vacate the cone, then punish the grounded pause.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Wildcats pressure low cover while the Lynx controls the high angle, but both share punishable landings.

monsters.name: Panther
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Move through connected dark cover and isolate one target by threatening allies who cross its marked line.
monsters.teachingGoal: Introduce a positioning specialist whose still eye line controls movement without magical disappearance.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Unbroken Gaze: the Panther marks a line between its visible eyes and prey, then strikes the first other target to cross it.
monsters.telegraph: Shoulder rosettes vanish sequentially into cover while the reflective eyes remain fixed and visible.
monsters.counterplay: Flood the line with a deliberate feint or attack the still eye position before moving the isolated target.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Wildcats occupy nearby low cover and Lynxes threaten the elevated route around the marked line.

monsters.name: Sabercat
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Commit both long canines to a ground pin that gives lesser Cats safer approach angles.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to exploit a champion's strongest weapon as a temporary anchor and weak point.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Twin-Canine Pin: both sabers plant beside the target and cannot withdraw until the Sabercat resets its forequarters.
monsters.telegraph: Its jaws open fully, forepaws widen, and heavy shoulders rise before the leap.
monsters.counterplay: Dodge inside the leap and punish the planted canines or exposed ribs before withdrawal.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Wildcats and Lynxes use the pin's open sides while the Panther holds the direct rescue line.

monsters.name: Pride Sovereign
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Divide the arena into stalking, pursuit, sightline, and pinning territories before leading a final crossing hunt.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test cover reading, vertical facing, eye-line control, and pin recovery in a staged apex hunt.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Four Hunting Grounds: the Sovereign traces a territory edge and assigns one lower Cat's rule to it before personally crossing the last open boundary.
monsters.telegraph: Its asymmetric mane and tail trace the next boundary while the assigned lower Cat takes a visible position.
monsters.counterplay: Disrupt the assigned Cat to open that boundary, then move through it before the Sovereign crosses.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Wildcat defines stalking cover, Lynx defines high ground, Panther defines the sightline, and Sabercat defines the pin territory; removing one permanently opens its ground.

monsters.name: Adder
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Coil once and strike exactly one body length.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to estimate a fixed biological strike range from the visible coil.
monsters.signatureMechanic: One-Length Strike: the Adder's extension never exceeds the length stored in its single tight coil.
monsters.telegraph: Its neck forms a tight S and the forked tongue stops flicking.
monsters.counterplay: Step beyond the fixed reach and punish the fully extended neck.

monsters.name: Constrictor
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Loop around one obstacle or target and tighten only while its head remains anchored.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to distinguish the dangerous body loop from the vulnerable head anchor.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Anchored Coil: a completed tail loop tightens while the jaws maintain one visible anchor point.
monsters.telegraph: The tail completes a circle and the jaw clamps firmly onto its anchor.
monsters.counterplay: Break the loop or stagger the anchored head to release all constriction pressure.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Adders threaten the predictable outside edge while the Constrictor holds the central loop.

monsters.name: Spitting Cobra
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Paint two visible venom lanes and threaten a conventional strike through the remaining gap.
monsters.teachingGoal: Introduce a ranged specialist that edits escape geometry while preserving a physical throat and hood tell.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Two-Fang Fan: each fang projects one narrow venom line, leaving a deliberate central or outer gap for the follow-up strike.
monsters.telegraph: Hood spots align with the two lanes and venom gathers separately at both fangs.
monsters.counterplay: Close behind the hood or bait both spits away from the escape route before crossing.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Adders guard the chosen gap while Constrictors anchor obstacles that narrow the available lanes.

monsters.name: Horned Viper
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Attack through alternating horn-marked emergence points while its exposed tail controls the safe route.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to infer the true buried head position from the deliberately misleading tail direction.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Horn Gates: paired eye horns surface at alternating points while the tail indicates the gap opposite the real opening.
monsters.telegraph: One horn breaks the surface before each head strike and the exposed tail points away from it.
monsters.counterplay: Follow the tail direction to locate the real opening and punish the emerging neck after evading.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Adders occupy abandoned horn points, Constrictors hold the center, and the Cobra paints lanes toward the false opening.

monsters.name: Crown Serpent
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Encircle the arena in layered body coils and assign lower Serpents to the gaps between them.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test fixed reach, head-anchor disruption, venom lanes, and buried emergence while treating the boss body as readable terrain.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Crown Coil: one crown scale lifts for each tightening body ring; the lower Serpent guarding that gap defines how it closes.
monsters.telegraph: Crown scales lift in the order of the next constriction and the corresponding lower Serpent becomes still.
monsters.counterplay: Remove or displace the still guard, cross the loosened coil, and strike the lifted crown scale before tightening resumes.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Adder supplies the fixed strike gap, Constrictor the anchored ring, Cobra the venom lane, and Horned Viper the buried opening; losing one permanently loosens its coil.

monsters.name: Mire Caiman
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Submerge along one visible ripple and snap once at the bank.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to track an aquatic ambush by its wake instead of staring at the last visible body position.
monsters.signatureMechanic: V-Wake Snap: the Caiman's eyes sink but its wake points continuously toward the fixed bank endpoint.
monsters.telegraph: The eyes submerge while a narrow V-shaped wake remains visible.
monsters.counterplay: Move parallel to the bank and punish the exposed tail after the missed snap.

monsters.name: River Crocodile
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Lunge a short distance, clamp one target, and drag backward without turning.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to escape the jaw line or attack the planted towing limbs instead of the armored back.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Parallel-Groove Drag: the Crocodile's foreclaws cut two fixed grooves that define its backward towing path.
monsters.telegraph: The jaw opens low and both foreclaws dig parallel grooves into the bank.
monsters.counterplay: Sidestep the jaws or strike the planted forelegs during the backward drag.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Mire Caimans threaten adjacent bank points while the Crocodile commits to its straight drag.

monsters.name: Snarejaw
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Sweep an elongated jaw around cover, close behind a target, and drag laterally along the shoreline.
monsters.teachingGoal: Introduce a qualitative lateral grab that rewards moving toward the hinge rather than away from the teeth.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Crescent Snare: the far jaw tip traces a semicircle around cover before the hinge closes and drags sideways.
monsters.telegraph: The far jaw tip taps the ground and the flexible neck bends into a visible crescent.
monsters.counterplay: Step toward the head hinge or strike the narrow jaw side before closure.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Caimans occupy nearby water exits while River Crocodiles threaten the straight retreat from the crescent.

monsters.name: Bastion Alligator
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Present a scute wall and commit to a fixed-direction death roll that exposes its softer belly at regular intervals.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to read rotational direction and wait for a repeating armor gap rather than attacking the back.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Three-Beat Roll: locked side scutes protect two beats and expose the pale belly fault on the second rotation.
monsters.telegraph: Side scutes lock together and the tail curves strongly against the coming rotation.
monsters.counterplay: Evade away from the tail curve and strike the belly fault during the second roll.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Lower Crocodilians drive targets toward the roll lane but must also avoid its predictable rotating body.

monsters.name: Primeval Crocodile
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Open and close three water channels, route lesser Crocodilians into bank attacks, then cross the arena with a colossal roll.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test wake tracking, clamp anchors, crescent grabs, and roll direction while the arena alternates wet and dry routes.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Three Flood Channels: the Primeval strikes channel gates in order, raising one hunting route and drying another before its crossing roll.
monsters.telegraph: Its tail strikes the next channel gate and the corresponding waterline rises before any lower form enters.
monsters.counterplay: Block the lower Crocodilian assigned to that channel, then use the resulting dry bank against the crossing roll.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Caimans reveal active wakes, River Crocodiles drag along straight banks, Snarejaw controls bends, and the Bastion Alligator occupies the final roll channel; disabling one preserves its dry route.

monsters.name: Carrion Kite
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Circle once and dive when its shadow crosses the target.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to track an aerial threat through the ground shadow and punish the low recovery climb.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Shadow Crossing: the Kite commits exactly when its tightening shadow touches the target's feet.
monsters.telegraph: The shadow tightens and the wings briefly stop beating.
monsters.counterplay: Step across the shadow and punish the Kite during its low recovery climb.

monsters.name: Hunting Hawk
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Alternate two shallow dives from opposite directions and perch after the second.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach players to update facing between attacks and recognize a guaranteed grounded recovery.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Paired Passes: the Hawk's tail points toward the next opposite-side pass before both attacks, followed by a fixed perch.
monsters.telegraph: Its tail fans toward the approach and the primary feathers whistle before each pass.
monsters.counterplay: Change facing between dives and attack the clearly selected perch after the second.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Kites cross the ground shadow while the Hawk demands alternating vertical facing.

monsters.name: Night Owl
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Track movement rather than position and drop onto the last target that sprinted.
monsters.teachingGoal: Introduce a qualitative specialist that changes safe movement cadence instead of merely adding another dive.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Last Motion Drop: the Owl fixes on the most recent sprint and descends silently onto that endpoint.
monsters.telegraph: Its facial disc narrows and airborne dust stops moving beneath its approach.
monsters.counterplay: Walk or hold still until the drop commits, then punish the open talons at ground contact.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Kite shadows encourage premature movement and Hawk passes alternate facing before the Owl selects the last sprint.

monsters.name: War Eagle
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Grip and lift one target a short distance while lesser Raptors attack the exposed group below.
monsters.teachingGoal: Teach parties to interrupt a visible lift quickly or use its predictable landing route for a coordinated punish.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Committed Carry: lowered talons grip once, follow one shadow-marked ascent lane, and return through one fixed landing route.
monsters.telegraph: Its legs lower, primary feathers spread, and the ascent lane lengthens in its shadow.
monsters.counterplay: Break the grip before lift or attack the predictable landing route when the Eagle returns.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Lower Raptors pressure the group during the lift but must clear the Eagle's fixed return lane.

monsters.name: Roc
monsters.battlefieldDuty: Create alternating high, crosswind, and ground-skimming flight bands before a full-span arena dive.
monsters.teachingGoal: Test ground-shadow reading, alternating facing, movement restraint, and landing-route interruption across vertical space.
monsters.signatureMechanic: Three Flight Bands: successive feather rows lift to assign a lower Raptor to one altitude band before the Roc seals the remaining band with its own dive.
monsters.telegraph: One feather row rises and its assigned bird calls once while the matching air lane gathers debris.
monsters.counterplay: Clear the assigned bird to create a safe vertical pocket before the Roc commits to the other bands.
monsters.lowerFormInteraction: Kite controls the shadow band, Hawk the crossing band, Owl the still-air band, and War Eagle the landing band; defeating one permanently opens its altitude pocket.

entries.rationale: Retain the plate-closing chokepoint tank as a bridge-only Arachnid role. None of the five primary forms combines its armored shove duty and lateral leg-joint counterplay, so assigning it to Broodmother or Weaver would erase a useful identity. Existing candidates remain ineligible because they do not establish a canonical form duty, anatomy, or framing contract.

Consolidate the egg-cluster spawner into the T4 Broodmother: both identities visibly carry brood, telegraph deployment through the abdomen, and expose that apparatus while producing spiderlings. Existing candidates remain ineligible because the canonical form adds a humanoid torso, three carried sacs, silk robes, and zone-command framing that the old giant-spider composition did not prove.

Consolidate the pure-spider low flanker into the T2 Stalker, preserving barbed legs, venom pressure, lateral ambush movement, and a soft abdomen punish window while adding the authored tripline lesson. Existing candidates remain ineligible because they were not framed to show the tripline duty or the canonical bright-abdomen telegraph across all five target affinities.

Retain the pure-spider ranged restraint role as bridge-only. The canonical T3 Weaver is the family's first humanoid-torso Specialist and rewrites existing lines rather than merely casting one, so this class cannot claim that primary coordinate. Existing candidates remain ineligible because their anatomy, battlefield duty, and single-cast framing contradict the Weaver form contract.

Retain the marked-target debuff skirmisher as a bridge-only hostile duty. Arcane hostiles are an occupational grouping rather than one of the thirty biological or constructed primary families, and no canonical form shares its three-tag casting grammar. Existing candidates remain ineligible until a bridge target defines stable family, form, anatomy, duty, and framing.

Retain the multi-school, multi-phase commander as a bridge-only tower role. Its identity is a combat office with changing magical schools rather than a member of a canonical monster family. Existing candidates remain ineligible until a separate bridge packet locks the phase duty, caster anatomy, focus telegraphs, and boss framing.

Retain the gate-building reinforcement controller as a bridge-only tower role. Its pylon channel is an occupational spell grammar that does not match any canonical family's authored lower-form production identity. Existing candidates remain ineligible until the bridge target fixes summoner anatomy, gate duty, pylon counterplay, and safe full-body framing.
